#### P14.T50 Elements and redox

`planetary/chem/`. T50.a and T50.c are on the snapshot path; T50.b is on the Surface path, built
only with an `envelope` section and read by T52.a and T52.d (decision-p14-t50b-envelope §4).

- **P14.T50.a Elements, reservoirs, redox and the new draws** (22 → 23).
  - **The element registry** (`substance/element.rs`): the 25 elements of Provides, each with:
    - its standard atomic weight;
    - its protosolar abundance from Lodders 2010 (the series this plan's disc already uses,
      Lodders 2003's Table 11), whose solar C/O is 0.457. Asplund et al. 2021's photospheric
      0.59 ± 0.08 is the recorded alternative, an uncertainty in every envelope's C/O (Risks);
    - its 50% condensation temperature (Lodders 2003, from memory).
  - **`ElementInventory`** (`chem/inventory.rs`) replaces `VolatileInventory`.
    - It holds masses per element (H, He, C, N, O, S, Cl, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe) and per reservoir
      (`Exchangeable`: the air, the surface's ices and liquids, and the crust's stored carbonate;
      `Mantle`).
    - Today's water, CO₂, N₂ and radiogenic ⁴⁰Ar are kept as its stored carriers, so
      `VolatileInventory`, now a view, returns today's values to the bit.
    - Sulphur and chlorine are log-normal multiples of the bulk silicate Earth's per unit mass
      (the builder cites a compilation, e.g. McDonough and Sun 1995, from memory), with 0.5 dex of
      scatter, the lane's and provisional as the others are. A body formed beyond the snow line
      takes chlorine at CI chondrites' abundance per unit mass of its rock instead (Lodders 2003,
      about 700 ppm, from memory, checked at build), with the same scatter: the bulk silicate Earth
      is depleted in chlorine against chondrites, and an icy body's rock is not. P14.T51.g's oceans
      leach it.
    - The primordial noble gases come at a cited chondritic or solar ratio per unit mass, with no
      draw.
  - **ΔIW** (`chem/redox.rs`): the present upper mantle's oxygen fugacity relative to the
    iron–wüstite buffer at its melting conditions, in log₁₀ units.
    - It is not core formation's, which differs (Earth about IW−2.2 then, near FMQ now).
    - Its deterministic mean is a function of the formation zone against the host's soot and snow
      lines, the water fraction, and the mass, the last standing for a deep magma ocean's Fe³⁺
      (Armstrong et al. 2019, from memory). A drawn scatter is added.
    - It is calibrated on the Solar System table:
      - Mercury IW−2.6 to −6.3 (McCubbin et al. 2012) and −4.5 to −7.3 (Zolotov et al. 2013);
      - the Moon IW+0.2 to −2.5 (Fogel and Rutherford 1995; Wadhwa 2008);
      - Mars's mantle close to IW (Wadhwa 2001);
      - Earth's upper mantle within ±2 log units of FMQ (Frost and McCammon 2008).
    - The FMQ–IW offset comes from the builder's cited buffer equations at a stated temperature,
      about 3.5 at 1,200–1,300 °C (from memory, not verified).
    - `RedoxClass` (`Reduced`, `Intermediate`, `Oxidised`) is a banding of ΔIW, with edges cited
      by T51.c. Enstatite chondrites and aubrites lie below IW−3 (Keil 2010, via Renggli et al.
      2024).
  - **The host's C/O and Mg/Si**: log(C/O) and log(Mg/Si) are the edition's solar values plus a
    trend in [Fe/H] and a scatter (Brewer and Fischer 2016, from memory: none of 849 FGK dwarfs
    reaches C/O 0.8), drawn per system, since siblings share their star's composition.
  - **The draws:**
    - `VolatileDraws` gains `sulphur`, `chlorine` and `redox`, words 3, 4 and 5 of
      `planet.volatiles`, read by `Stream::word_at`, so words 0–2 and every existing value are
      untouched. `VOLATILE_WORDS` stays 8, and `MEDIAN` sets each to one half.
    - A new tag, `system.abundances` (System scope, appended under this plan's heading after
      `body.surface.detail`), holds word 0, the host's C/O rank, and word 1, its Mg/Si rank, with
      words 2–7 reserved (`ABUNDANCE_WORDS` = 8). It is keyed by `ObjectKey::from(SystemId)` so
      that every body of a system reads one value, until plan 06 carries the ratios on the star.
  - _Tests:_
    - H₂O, CO₂, N₂ and Ar as today, to the bit (every golden unchanged by this subtask);
    - Earth's, Venus's and Mars's sulphur within stated ranges, from cited inventories;
    - the elements sum to the carriers at 10⁻⁹;
    - the table's Mercury, Moon, Mars and Earth within their cited ΔIW;
    - ΔIW continuous in its inputs;
    - the draws' golden (words 3–5, and `system.abundances` words 0–1);
    - two bodies of one system read one C/O;
    - the same seed gives the same draws twice.
  - _Files:_ `substance/element.rs`, `planetary/chem/{mod, inventory, redox}.rs`,
    `planetary/derive/atmosphere.rs`, `rng/tags.rs` (`tags.golden` gains its line), and the
    draws' test and golden.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive::atmosphere`; `cargo test -p hyperion-sim rng::tags`.
  - _The planets' nitrogen_ is P14.T50.c's (decision-p14-moons, §F1-plan). This subtask keeps
    every carrier to the bit.
- **P14.T50.b A gas envelope's element abundances** (23 → 24, updated 2026-10-15; read by
  T52.d).
  - `chem/envelope_abundances.rs`: for a body in `SurfaceState::GasEnvelope`, its abundances by
    number relative to H, of He, C, N, O, S, P, Na, K, Ti, V, Fe, Mg, Si, Ca, Al, Cl, Cr, Mn, Ni
    and Zn (Cr, Mn and Zn are the limiting elements of T52.c's `Cr`, `MnS` and `ZnS` decks, and
    all four have visible lines; science-r08-unowned-absorbers):
    - every element of `Element::ALL` (these 21 with Ne, Ar, Kr and Xe), by number relative to H;
    - the metals are the host's (protosolar × 10^[Fe/H], the α elements × 10^[α/Fe], carbon at the
      host's C/O and magnesium at its Mg/Si, T50.a) times E(M) = 2.65 (M ÷ M_J)^−0.986, the four
      giants' measured C/H (Guillot et al. 2022, Table 2). E is at most the radius model's bulk
      metal fraction (Thorngren et al. 2016; Thorngren and Fortney 2019, f ≤ 1) and at least 1;
    - C/O is the host's times the disc gas's C/O by zone over the disc's (Öberg, Murray-Clay and
      Bergin 2011, Table 1: CO, CO₂, water at the snow line, carbon grains at the soot line,
      silicates), at the C+N+O mass E gives. N/O is protosolar;
    - He/H is the envelope's primordial value, depleted by helium rain in a gas giant of at least
      0.15 M_J. The rain is linear in Hubbard's T₀ ∝ g^−0.167 T_eff^1.243 through Jupiter's and
      Saturn's measured helium, from none at 0.7 Gyr to all of it at 1.5 Gyr. Neon falls with the
      helium; a sub-Neptune or an ice giant keeps its helium.
  - _Tests:_
    - Jupiter's C/H within a factor of 2 of the Galileo probe's (about four times solar, from
      memory) at its E(M);
    - a 10 M⊕ sub-Neptune's metallicity of order 100 × solar;
    - the abundances sum consistently with E(M) to 10⁻⁹;
    - C/O at median ranks is the host's times the ice-line factor.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/chem/envelope_abundances.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::envelope_abundances`.
- **P14.T50.c The ammonia line for nitrogen** (22 → 23; lane `p14-snapshot`, after T50.a and
  before T51.a; amends T13.a; decision-p14-moons §2 and §F1-plan).
  - **The defect.** `ICY_VOLATILE_BOOST` (100) raises a body's nitrogen wherever water condenses.
    But nitrogen's icy carrier, ammonia monohydrate, appears only at 131 K and holds half of all
    nitrogen only by 123 K (Lodders 2003, ApJ 591, 1220, Table 8 and §3.4.3, at 10⁻⁴ bar; read).
    Titan's nitrogen, by which the boost was calibrated, came as NH₃ (Mousis, Gautier and
    Bockelée-Morvan 2002, Icarus 156, 162, not read; Mandt et al. 2014, ApJ 788, L24, abstract
    read).
  - **The rule.** `AMMONIA_HYDRATE_CONDENSATION` = 123 K, nitrogen's 50% condensation
    temperature, `Element::N`'s (T50.a) (`derive/atmosphere.rs`), and
    `nitrogen_boosted(formation_temperature) -> bool`, true at or below it. A body's nitrogen takes
    `ICY_VOLATILE_BOOST` only where its formation temperature is at most 123 K, and Earth's per
    unit mass times its rank otherwise.
    - A planet's, dwarf planet's or belt member's formation temperature is its star disc's under
      the disc's Hayashi profile at its formation distance: T_f = 170 K × √(d_snow ÷ d_form),
      with d_snow the disc's snow line. So the boost begins at (170 ÷ 123)² = 1.910 d_snow:
      4.32 au about the zero-age Sun, 5.16 √L au about a host of zero-age luminosity L.
    - A moon's is P14.T56.c's.
    - A body that migrated keeps its formation distance's value, as its snow-line side does.
    - Water and carbon keep the snow line (170 K), as built. Nitrogen inside the snow line is
      unchanged.
    - `ElementInventory`'s nitrogen carrier (T50.a) follows `VolatileInventory`'s.
  - **Held** behind `AMMONIA_LINE_VERSION` = 23 (`derive/atmosphere.rs`), as T14.d was behind
    `ENVELOPED_TIDES_VERSION`. Below 23 every inventory is version 22's, bit for bit, and a
    tripwire test fails once the version reaches 23. T54.a deletes both.
  - _Tests:_
    - `AMMONIA_HYDRATE_CONDENSATION` is 123 K, equal to `Element::N.condensation_temperature()`,
      with its source;
    - about the zero-age Sun's disc (0.7 L☉), the ammonia line lies at 1.910 times the snow line,
      4.32 ± 0.01 au;
    - a body formed at 3 au has Earth's nitrogen per unit mass at its rank, and one formed at
      5 au 100 times it; their water and carbon equal version 22's, bit for bit;
    - a body formed inside the snow line is unchanged, bit for bit;
    - the atmosphere table: Ceres's nitrogen falls a hundredfold and it stays airless; Mercury,
      Venus, Earth, Mars, the Moon, Ganymede and Titan are unchanged, bit for bit;
    - the boost is a step in formation distance only, so every body's inventory stays continuous
      in time;
    - the hold: below 23, every golden is unchanged, bit for bit.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/derive/atmosphere.rs` (`volatile_inventory`, the constant, the hold),
    `planetary/derive/atmosphere/tests.rs`, `planetary/chem/inventory.rs` (the carrier follows).
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive::atmosphere`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem`.
  - _Moves at 23 (estimated):_
    - every solid body formed between 1 and 1.910 snow-line distances (0.28 dex of formation
      distance) keeps 1% of its version-22 nitrogen: planets, dwarf planets, belt members and,
      through T56.c, captured moons of parents formed there;
    - where such a body keeps an N₂-dominated air (a migrated icy or ocean world, or a snowball
      formed there), its N₂ pressure falls a hundredfold and its nitrogen greenhouse term tenfold.
      Its surface temperature and photometry follow, and the thinnest cross the 100 Pa airless
      line;
    - gas envelopes do not move: T50.b's N/O governs them;
    - nothing inside the snow line or beyond the ammonia line moves;
    - goldens: the `planetary/systems` goldens with such bodies, and Ceres's row of the table.
      T54.a's bless note counts them.
- **P14.T50.d An envelope's formation draws** (23 → 24 as a rider; otherwise the next planetary
  bump; after T50.b; decision-p14-t50b-envelope §1–2, 2026-10-16).
  - E's scatter as a rank-drawn log-normal about the trend, within the bound and the floor. σ is
    stated against the giants' residuals and JWST's spread at fixed mass; Thorngren et al.'s ×1.82
    bulk spread is the reference.
  - The solids' share of the envelope's C, N and O as a rank, between the gas-phase factor (as
    built) and Öberg's Eq. 2 with the zone's own solids (Espinoza et al. 2017). It is calibrated so
    the giants' C/O spans JWST's measurements (HD 189733 b < 0.2; Fu et al. 2025), with the Solar
    System's four giants inside the central 68%. The builder tests a lean towards solids for hot
    Jupiters.
  - A new Body-scope tag: `planet.volatiles` words 6–7 are reserved for phosphorus and isotopes.

#### P14.T51 Surface composition

- **P14.T51.a The condensate partition** (22 → 23; amends T24.a–b and T48.d).
  - `chem/partition.rs`, called inside T13's three passes after escape and before the greenhouse.
  - For each registry condensable the exchangeable inventory carries, in registry order:
    - **The vapour pressure.** A condensable that dominates its air takes its saturation pressure
      at the coldest zone (T24.a's `climate_range`, its coldest, where its reservoir cold-traps,
      after Wordsworth 2015, as T48.d already cites) (methane included: a cold world
      whose methane at T24.f's 0.5 would exceed its background, which T24.f holds at 0.5
      meanwhile; science-p14-t24f §2). A minor one in a non-condensing
      background takes the mean temperature with T24.c's surface humidity. Either way the cap is
      on its partial pressure in the air, x_s p ≤ h p_sat,s(T) (h = 1 at a dominant condensable's
      cold trap, T24.c's humidity for a minor one), x_s its mole fraction and p the summed weights.
      Its airborne weight w_s is the smaller of M_s g ÷ 4πR² and the weight that meets the cap,
      never the cap applied to the weight itself: for water in nitrogen the two differ by a factor
      of 1.6 (signoff-3.md, item 1.7). The change from the minor branch to
      the dominant one is continuous in the condensable's share of the air (a weight the builder
      states and cites, not a switch), since the gases are continuous in time but at recorded state
      changes. Titan, at 5.7% methane, stays on the minor branch within its test.
    - **The CO₂ of dry worlds beyond the maximum-greenhouse limit** (science-p14-t24f, finding 1).
      A rocky world formed inside the snow line that lies beyond the limit stores no carbon, since
      no ocean weathers it, and its median 70 bar of CO₂ runs T13.c's √p greenhouse away to
      490–575 K, labelled `Snowball` (T13.c's findings), where Kopparapu et al. 2013 and Kasting,
      Whitmire and Reynolds 1993 put any CO₂ air below 273 K. This cold-trap rule is the planned
      fix: such a world's CO₂ is the dominant condensable, held at `p_sat`(T_cold) with T48.e's
      contrasts, as Mars's is after Wordsworth 2015.
    - **The condensed reservoir**, M_s − w_s 4πR² ÷ g, as a global equivalent layer.
    - **Its phase** where it lies: solid below the triple point (or the eutectic, for a
      solution); liquid inside its window at the surface pressure; supercritical above T_c and
      p_c, with no interface; `seasonal` where the warmest zone rises above the frost point.
  - **Published as `Condensates`:** at most eight
    `{ substance, phase, reservoir_gel_m, area_fraction, seasonal }`, sorted by reservoir mass,
    with ties by `SubstanceId`.
    - T24.b's `surface_liquids` take each liquid's logistic of volume over the basin capacity,
      summing to the ocean fraction.
    - Its `surface_ices` take each solid's area.
    - T24.a's liquid-water flag is derived from them.
    - T48.d's condensable is, of the condensables whose phase changes inside the climate's range,
      the one with the largest partial pressure in the air (P14.T48.d, signoff-3.md).
  - _Tests_ (the Solar System table):
    - Earth holds liquid and solid water;
    - a Mars given its measured 6 mbar of CO₂ by hand holds perennial and seasonal CO₂ ice and
      water ice (the generated Mars stores its carbon in rock until T53.a, a finding the test
      records);
    - Titan (after T24.f) holds liquid CH₄ over a water-ice crust;
    - a Triton and a Pluto given their measured N₂, CH₄ and CO by hand hold N₂ ice with CH₄, and
      their CH₄ partial pressure within a factor of 3 of the measured (about 10⁻³ Pa on Triton,
      (3–8) × 10⁻³ Pa on Pluto, from memory, to an order of magnitude; from methane-rich terrain
      warmer than the N₂ ice; science-p14-t24f §1);
    - a cold world of 0.2 bar of N₂ at 120 K holds its methane at `p_sat`(T_cold), within 10% (by
      hand, with its contrasts);
    - an Earth formed inside the snow line at 2 au of a Sun holds its CO₂ at the cold trap, its
      surface below 273 K;
    - Venus holds none, and at 92 bar given by hand a supercritical CO₂ surface;
    - a 10-bar CO₂ world at 250 K holds a liquid-CO₂ sea;
    - for every species, airborne and condensed masses sum to the inventory to 10⁻⁹;
    - a minor condensable's partial pressure x_s p equals h p_sat,s to 10⁻⁹ where it is capped;
    - continuous in time but at recorded state changes;
    - the partition's pressures replace the mean-temperature caps only for dominant condensables;
      the bless note lists the bodies whose surface pressure moves.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/chem/partition.rs`, `planetary/derive/atmosphere.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::partition`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive::atmosphere`.
- **P14.T51.b The area-mix Bond albedo** (22 → 23; amends T13.c's table and T47's choice of p;
  after T51.a, P14.T49.c and P14.T49.h's step 1).
  - Inside the three passes, A = Σ aᵢAᵢ over:
    - the crust's regolith;
    - each condensate's area at its Bond albedo:
      - a solid's from P14.T49.c's spherical albedo by band, never its A_N, a radiance factor;
      - a liquid's from P14.T49.h's record: the cosine-weighted Fresnel reflectance r_d(n) =
        2∫R_F(μ) μ dμ (water's 0.066, against 0.020 at normal incidence), plus the body's light,
        (1 − r_d)(1 − r_i) R∞ ÷ (1 − r_i R∞), with R∞ = 0.33 b_b ÷ (a + b_b) (Morel and
        Prieur 1977) and r_i the interface's internal diffuse reflectance;
      - the body term absent where a or b is: a deep, flat, pure liquid, stated
        (decision-p14-t49c-split §2);
    - the cloud term, the snapshot path's cloud fraction times the cloud albedo of the state.
      That cloud fraction comes from the state and the condensable's availability (a runaway world
      with sulphur keeps 1; a dry, thin-aired world falls to the condensable's), never from the
      Surface path's decks.
  - Each component's Bond albedo weights its band albedos by the host's flux in each band's edges
    (a Planck curve at T_eff, or the sim's stellar spectrum where it reaches, stated), over the
    bands the optics carry. These are B, V and R until P14.T49.i adds the infrared, whose commit
    asserts the anchors that need it.
  - A row with no condensed optics takes a labelled stand-in the builder states, never a silent
    default.
  - Until P14.T54.b weathers the area mix (R10.T1.d's law over P14.T51.d's maturity and rate;
    decision-p14-t51d-weathering), an airless body's silicate crust takes the smaller of its row's
    Bond albedo and the Moon's measured 0.11 (NASA's fact sheet, T13.c's present value), labelled
    as a stand-in for space weathering. P14.T54.b deletes the rule.
  - Its call into `condensed_optics` sits behind the lane's hold, and its file joins T49.c's
    tripwire's held list.
  - **The passes take the record's composition** (science-p14-t24a-climate.md §6, item 3): the
    material and the crust that a body's bulk section states, not its placement's.
    - That composition is fixed before the passes for an icy belt member (`icy_member_bulk`), a
      regular moon (`DerivedMoon::fractions`, its ice fraction), a giant-impact moon and a capture
      (`moon_bulk_of`). It depends on the mass, the radius rank, the circumplanetary ice line, a
      capture's radius or the parent's derivation, so `derive_body` takes it as an input:
      P14.T56.c's follow-up's `PlacedBody::with_bulk` and `GivenBulk`, which this subtask extends to
      `icy_member_bulk`'s members, and for a moon `derive_moon`'s `MoonBulk`. No second bulk input
      is added, and the albedo reads the fractions the air reads (decision-triton-and-e101 §1.7).
    - `DerivedBody::albedo` then equals the photometry section's Bond albedo for every body. That
      retires P14.T47's exception (Risks, "Deviations in P14.T47.a–c", _The Bond albedo_).
    - T24.a's regolith inertia then sits over the same material's albedo.
  - **A gas envelope's Bond albedo** comes from its class by T_eq, closed form: Sudarsky, Burrows
    and Pinto 2000's Table 1a gives class I 0.57, II 0.81, III 0.12, IV 0.03 and V 0.55 about a
    G2V star. They are host-dependent: class I runs from 0.63 about an A8V star to 0.38 about an
    M4V, so the host's T_eff enters by their table. They are accurate to about 10–15%. Interpolated
    in T_eq across each class boundary, so that the albedo and T_eq converge in the three passes.
  - The phase template's p follows the new Bond albedo (T47's rule).
  - _Tests:_
    - the Moon's 0.11 kept, by the space-weathering stand-in; Mercury's 0.088, the bolometric Bond
      albedo (Mallama 2017), and its 0.068 in V move to P14.T54.b (decision-p14-t51d-weathering
      §3);
    - Earth's 0.294 and Venus's 0.76 kept by their calibrations;
    - a Pluto and a Triton given their measured N₂, CH₄ and CO by hand (T51.a's fixtures) take a
      Bond albedo within 0.6–0.8 and 0.72–0.92: Buratti et al. 2017 (Icarus 287, 207) give Pluto
      0.72 ± 0.07 and Hillier et al. 1990 (Science 250, 419) Triton 0.82 ± 0.05, both read
      (decision-triton-and-e101 §1.6). At their own inventories both are `Airless` with no N₂
      until P14.T53.c, which the test records rather than asserts. Triton's N₂ pressure, 1.4 Pa,
      is P14.T53.c's test: it is set by the ice's own temperature and emissivity, not by this
      albedo (asserted from P14.T49.i's commit, which adds the bands they need);
    - an Enceladus near 0.8 (Howett et al. 2010, from memory) (asserted from P14.T49.i's commit,
      which adds the bands they need);
    - a 1,200 K giant between class IV's and V's albedos, and Jupiter's within 0.05 of its table
      value;
    - an icy belt member whose placement holds under 10% water, a capture whose density makes it
      icy, and a giant-impact moon of a rocky planet each take the albedo, and so the T_eq, of their
      bulk section's material;
    - over the sample, `DerivedBody::albedo` equals the photometry section's Bond albedo to the
      bit;
    - the passes converge to 10⁻⁹ in T_eq.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/derive/{atmosphere, photometry}.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive` and
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim --lib -- planetary::chem::partition planetary::moons::regular planetary::system::tests::under_the_batch`
    (widened as built: the tests the first filter does not reach).
- **P14.T51.c Crust composition, redox class and melt area** (22 → 23; after T50.a).
  - `hooks/crust.rs`:
    `CrustComposition { primary: Option<SubstanceId>, secondary: Option<SubstanceId>, tertiary: Option<SubstanceId>, bulk: Option<SubstanceId>, lid: LidCrust, provinces: SubstanceId, redox: RedoxClass, melt_area_fraction: f64 }`
    and `LidCrust { Primary, Secondary, Bulk }`. The inputs are:
    - T50.a's ΔIW, water fraction and host Mg/Si;
    - T48.a's f_c;
    - T24.b's heat flow, regime and surface age;
    - P14.T28.a's `molten_until` and formation time;
    - T56.d's tidal volcanism;
    - the body's radius and core mass fraction;
    - a formation time t_f (below).

    The crusts are the body's, buried or not; `lid` names the one at the surface. Either `bulk`
    is present alone, or at least one of `primary` and `secondary` is, and `lid` names a present
    member (science-r09-drainage.md §5; science-composition-crusts.md §1 and §5).

  - **The thermal history** decides between a crust and `bulk` (science-composition-crusts.md
    §1.4).
    - **The peak central temperature T_c,max** is that of a compact conductive sphere of the
      body's radius, heated from t_f by ²⁶Al and the long-lived nuclides in its rock. The
      eigenfunction series is summed over a fixed number of terms and times. Its constants
      (²⁶Al/²⁷Al, half-lives, decay energies, Al, K, Th and U contents, c and κ) are each
      stated with its source.
    - **t_f:**
      - a planet's is T28.a's;
      - a regular moon's is drawn uniform in [its giant's formation, L];
      - a belt member's, a captured moon's or a comet's is drawn uniform in [0, L], L being
        T28.a's disc lifetime;
      - the draws sit on a stream this task chooses under the determinism rules, so that no
        existing value moves.
    - **Rock melted, giving a crust** (the bullets below):
      - a planet;
      - a rocky parent's impact moon;
      - a tidally volcanic body (T56.d);
      - any body whose T_c,max reaches the chondritic solidus at low pressure, 1,423 K (1,150 °C:
        Jurewicz et al., LPSC 24, 1993, for H and LL chondrites at 1 atm and IW−1).
    - **Ice melted, rock not:** a body formed beyond the snow line whose T_c,max reaches the
      ice's melting point (273.15 K, or 176 K for NH₃–H₂O), plus the ice's latent heat.
      - At 200 km radius or more, its ocean froze into a primary crust (Ice crusts, below).
      - Smaller, it altered in place, giving `bulk`:
        - `cometary` where its surface keeps water ice (T51.a's airless branch at H₂O's 110 K
          threshold);
        - otherwise `chondrite_cv` where T_c,max reached 900 K;
        - otherwise `chondrite_ci` where its ice-to-rock mass ratio is at least 0.5;
        - otherwise `chondrite_cm`.
    - **Nothing melted, giving `bulk`:**
      - `cometary` beyond the snow line;
      - inside it, by `RedoxClass`: `chondrite_e` (`Reduced`); `chondrite_h`, `chondrite_l` or
        `chondrite_ll` from reduced to oxidised (`Intermediate`, at cited edges); `chondrite_ll`
        (`Oxidised`).
  - **Primary:**
    - a plagioclase flotation crust where a magma ocean existed on a body small enough for
      plagioclase to float (the Moon). It is named `feldspathic`, the crust as impacts have mixed
      it, with 4–5 wt% FeO; the rock `anorthosite` is its purest part.
    - Earth- and Mars-mass bodies get an ultramafic crust after overturn (Hu, Ehlmann and Seager
      2012, after Elkins-Tanton et al. 2005, the latter to be read at build).
    - On a reduced body, graphite flotation (Mercury's low-reflectance material).
    - A frozen ocean's shell is primary too: Ceres's altered, salt- and phyllosilicate-bearing
      crust, "the bulk of Ceres's original ocean" (Castillo-Rogez et al. 2018, p. 1838; Fu et al.
      2017), and an ocean world's ice shell.
  - **Secondary:** a solid mantle's partial melt. It is `None` where the mantle never melted (a
    Ceres, whose rock "avoided igneous differentiation", Fu et al. 2017). Where it exists, the
    first rule that applies gives it:
    1. `basalt_reduced` on a reduced body;
    2. `komatiite` where the mantle is hot (young, or radiogenically or tidally heated);
    3. `basalt_fe`, an iron-rich basalt (FeO about 18–22 wt%), where its source is iron-rich:
       - a magma ocean's cumulate mantle beneath a plagioclase flotation crust (the lunar maria);
       - or a mantle with at least 12 wt% FeO by mass balance, a Mars or a Vesta. That is
         1.2865 × max(0, w_Fe − f_core × 0.85) ÷ (1 − f_core), with w_Fe the bulk iron fraction
         from the host's Fe/(Mg + Si) and Mg/Si, and 0.85 the core's iron fraction. The 12 wt%
         is the geometric mean of the bulk silicate Earth's 8.05 wt% (McDonough and Sun 1995)
         and Mars's 17.9 (Dreibus and Wänke 1985), both to be read at build;
    4. `basalt` otherwise.

    Each is shifted towards silica-rich or Mg-rich by Mg/Si, which reaches Putirka and Xu 2021's
    exotic mantle rocks without a special case.

  - **Tertiary:** `granite` where f_c > 0, which already needs a mobile lid and surface water
    (Campbell and Taylor 1983).
  - **Ice crusts:** the primary crust of a body whose ice melted and whose ocean froze is:
    - `H2O` where ice is at least 0.3 of its mass, or its rock differentiated beneath the ocean
      (Europa);
    - `phyllosilicate` with its salts where rock is the larger part of its ocean's load (Ceres).

    Salts, NH₃ hydrate or clathrate are minor substances where the inventory carries them. An
    icy body that never melted has `bulk: cometary`, its ices being T51.a's and T51.f's
    condensates.

  - **Lid:**
    - `Bulk` on an undifferentiated body;
    - otherwise `Primary` where the body has a primary crust and nothing has resurfaced it since
      it formed: T24.b's surface age is at least the time since the magma ocean's end
      (`molten_until`), or since the ocean froze. That covers the Moon's highlands and a Ceres;
    - otherwise `Secondary`: Mars and Mercury, over their buried primary crusts, and Earth and
      Venus.
    - Where `lid` is `Primary`, a resurfaced share shows as provinces (R09's V).
  - **`melt_area_fraction`:** the surface's area above the solidus of the lid's crust, from the
    closed-form surface-temperature distribution. A locked airless world's is T_ss cos^¼θ, so a
    lava world has a dayside pool and a solid nightside (Léger et al. 2011; Kite et al. 2016).
    `MagmaOcean` stays the global state. R09.T13.c applies each cell's own entry's solidus.
  - **The provinces** are the lid's own substance on a body with no constructional volcanism.
  - **The regolith's thermal inertia** (science-p14-t24a-climate.md §6, item 2) is P14.T49.j's law
    at the lid this task gives, which P14.T54.a passes to T24.a. A body's dark, hydrated or icy
    regolith follows from its lid, with no class of its own.
  - _Tests:_
    - the Moon a `feldspathic` primary lid with `basalt_fe` provinces;
    - Mercury reduced and low-FeO: a `basalt_reduced` lid over a graphite primary crust;
    - Earth granitic continents on basaltic oceanic crust;
    - Venus a `basalt` stagnant lid;
    - Mars a `basalt_fe` lid over a buried ultramafic primary crust, with its ferric surface from
      P14.T51.j;
    - an icy body whose ice melted an `H2O` primary crust;
    - a Ceres-like body (470 km, a quarter water, t_f 3 Myr) a primary phyllosilicate crust and
      no secondary;
    - a hot young mantle komatiitic;
    - the secondary crust shifts with Mg/Si at fixed everything else, and an Earth's mass
      balance gives `basalt` and a Mars's `basalt_fe`;
    - a locked lava world's melt area is between 0 and 0.5 and rises with T_ss;
    - the `RedoxClass` bands cited;
    - the thermal history's anchors (science-composition-crusts.md §1.4):
      - a dry 100 km body at t_f 2.3 Myr has an ordinary-chondrite `bulk` (Henke et al. 2012);
      - a dry body of 60 km or more at 1.4 Myr has a crust (Hunt et al. 2018);
      - a 25 km body at 0.1 Myr has a crust (Neumann et al. 2023);
      - an icy 100 km body at 3 Myr melts its ice, and not after 4 Myr (Bland and Travis 2017);
      - a Pluto (1,190 km, a third ice, 5 Myr) has a primary `H2O` crust;
      - a 10 km icy body at 1 Myr or later, and a 200 km Kuiper-belt body at 5 Myr, are
        `cometary`;
      - a `Reduced` dry body that never melted is `chondrite_e`;
    - `bulk` excludes every crust; `lid` names a present member;
    - the series within 1% of 400 terms;
    - the formation time's draw is deterministic, and no existing value moves.
  - _Sources:_ Taylor and McLennan 2009; Hu, Ehlmann and Seager 2012; Campbell and Taylor 1983;
    Nittler et al. 2011; McCubbin et al. 2012; Peplowski et al. 2016; Putirka and Xu 2021 (the
    surfaces audit §2.1–2.3); Henke et al. 2012; Jurewicz et al. 1993 (LPSC 24, and GCA 57,
    2123); Hunt et al. 2018; Neumann et al. 2023; Bland and Travis 2017; Keil 2010; McDonough and
    Sun 1995; Dreibus and Wänke 1985 (science-composition-crusts.md).
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/crust.rs`, and the draw's tag (`rng/tags.rs` and `tags.golden`) if
    it takes a new one.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::crust`.
- **P14.T51.d Surface modifiers** (23 → 24).
  - `hooks/modifiers.rs`:
    - an irradiated-organics cover, for surfaces holding CH₄, N₂, CO or CH₃OH ices, from the UV and
      particle dose, giving a tholin cover;
    - a resurfacing rate from volcanism or tidal heat, which gives Io its SO₂ frost and sulphur
      from T24.g's outgassing.
  - _The units_ (decision-r11-palette-liquids §2 item 4, 2026-10-14): the maturity and the organic
    cover are dimensionless in [0, 1], maturity 0 for fresh ground and 1 for saturated space
    weathering, and the organic cover the covered fraction of the ground that can take one.
    P14.T54.b carries them to rendering plan R09's reserved header parts `maturity` and
    `organic_cover`. This task fixes their exact definitions inside that contract; a shape it cannot
    fit goes to "main" before T54.b. The resurfacing rate stays off the header, since the surface
    age carries it for R10 and R11.
  - a space-weathering maturity m and rate k (decision-p14-t51d-weathering §2, 2026-10-16):
    - m is the background regolith's npFe⁰ content as a fraction of the Moon's mature
      background's, per unit of FeO_T, which the shared law reads linearly;
    - m_body = 1 − exp(−k t_s ÷ τ_L), from
      `hyperion_surface::material::{body_maturity, LUNAR_MATURATION_TIME}`, which this task builds
      in `material/maturity.rs`, with τ_L fitted to Grier et al. 2001's Tycho and Copernicus;
    - k is the orbit-mean surface-reaching dose rate relative to the Moon's,
      k = 0.5 Φ_w ÷ Φ_w,Moon + 0.5 Φ_d ÷ Φ_d,Moon (the split labelled):
      - the wind's flux Ṁ ÷ (4π a² √(1 − e²)), times its unshielded share: 0 under air above
        T53.c's tenuous floor or inside a planet's magnetopause, and 1 − √(1 − R ÷ r_mp) under a
        dipole;
      - the micrometeoroids' n(r) v(r)³ ∝ r^(−1.3) (G M_* ÷ r)^(3/2) at a labelled dust level of
        1, times exp(−Σ ÷ 0.3 kg m⁻²) of the air's column;
    - k goes on `modifiers` as `weathering_rate`.
  - _Tests:_
    - the Moon's k = 1 to 10⁻¹² and m ≥ 0.99;
    - a magnetised twin has a lower k, and on a 100 Myr surface a lower m;
    - Mercury's k is above 1, its two terms printed, within Braden and Robinson 2013's ratio;
    - air above the tenuous floor gives no wind term, and Mars's k is below 0.01;
    - `maturity_after` at k = 1 is below 30 ÷ X at 109 Myr and above 60 ÷ X at 810 Myr, X being the
      lunar mature background's I_s/FeO;
    - a CH₄-ice body under a high dose carries a cover, and one without CH₄ none;
    - an `Extreme`-volcanism moon is resurfaced with SO₂ frost and sulphur.
  - The albedo anchors moved here by decision-p14-t49c-split §1.5 move on:
    - the Moon's highlands and maria to rendering plan R10.T1.d's calibration;
    - Mercury's two checks and Europa's in-range check to P14.T54.b.
  - _Sources:_ Hapke 2001; Pieters and Noble 2016; Vernazza et al. 2009; Cruikshank, Imanaka and
    Dalle Ore 2005; Brown, Schaller and Fraser 2011; Morris 1978; Grier et al. 2001; Cintala 1992;
    Leinert et al. 1981; Blewett et al. 2011; Braden and Robinson 2013.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/modifiers.rs`; `crates/hyperion-surface/src/material/maturity.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::modifiers`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-surface material::maturity`.
- **P14.T51.e Small bodies' surface types** (23 → 24; amends T21's members and T17–T19's small
  moons).
  - `hooks/small_bodies.rs`: a taxonomic class for the record and the census, a label and not a
    substance, derived from T51.c's lithology and T51.d's maturity and cover:
    - S (Q where fresh) for an ordinary chondrite;
    - C for `chondrite_ci` and `chondrite_cm`;
    - K or L for `chondrite_cv`;
    - Xc for `chondrite_e`;
    - V for a `basalt_fe` crust;
    - D for `cometary` under an organic cover, and P without;
    - red or neutral for a Kuiper-belt body by T51.d's cover.

    These pairings are from memory, to be read at build (DeMeo and Carry 2014; Nakamura et al.
    2011 for Itokawa's LL; science-composition-crusts.md §1.2). A rubble pile or a fragment takes
    its parent's lithology. If a zone mixes types, it draws on a tag of its own.

  - _Tests:_
    - inner-belt members S-type and outer C-type, in DeMeo and Carry 2014's proportion
      qualitatively;
    - a large differentiated member can be V-type;
    - a Kuiper-like member beyond the volatile line red, inside it neutral.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/small_bodies.rs`, one call each in `belts.rs` and `moons/`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::small_bodies`.
- **P14.T51.f Cold traps on airless bodies** (23 → 24; amends T51.a; science-r09-drainage.md §4;
  after rendering plan R09's R09.T7.d).
  - **Where:** `hooks/cold_traps.rs`, for a body with no collisional atmosphere.
  - **Which condensables:** each one its exchangeable inventory carries (T50.a), and H₂O and CO₂,
    which impactors deliver to any body.
  - **The cold-trap fraction:** the area fraction from `hyperion_surface::cold_trap::fraction`,
    integrated over latitude. This task calls it and does not build it: R09.T7.d builds it early,
    pure and in `f64` in the surface crate (the galaxy audit's B4), and R09.T13.f calls the same
    function to place the ice per cell. It is Hayne et al. 2021's template (Nat. Astron. 5, 169,
    eqs. 1 and 26), with Ingersoll, Svitek and Murray 1992's shadow temperature (Icarus 100, 40)
    at the star's highest elevation (R09.T7.d; science-r09-drainage.md §8).
    `cold_trap::permanent_shadow`, the same model without the temperature cut, serves the Ceres
    test. The fraction's inputs are:
    - the star's greatest declination in the body's sky, min(ε, 180° − ε) of the present
      obliquity to the seasonal orbit, labelled, since cold traps record the obliquity's history;
    - the star's angular radius and flux at periapsis, the Bond albedo, the emissivity, and the
      internal heat flow (T24.b), which sets the shadows' floor (about 24 K on the Moon) and decides
      N₂, CO and CH₄;
    - the crater fraction and d/D distribution (log-normal mean and variance) from the crater state;
    - the plains' directional RMS slope;
    - the share of the cold-trapping area under lateral conduction's cut-off, the lunar 0.05
      (labelled).
  - **The threshold of each species:** the temperature at which Hertz–Knudsen sublimation from its
    T49.b saturation curve is 144 kg m⁻² Gyr⁻¹ (Schorghofer and Williams 2020, PSJ 1, 54, Table 1:
    110 K for H₂O).
    It is one rule for every species. For CO₂ it gives about 57 K: Clausius–Clapeyron from the
    194.7 K sublimation point at 25–27 kJ mol⁻¹ gives 55.5–58.4 K, and T49.b's curve decides.
    Schorghofer et al. 2021's stricter 10 kg m⁻² Gyr⁻¹, a delivery rate, is 55.6 K on Bryson et
    al. 1974's vapour pressures (GRL 48, e2021GL095533, supplement; the LPSC 2021 abstract's "about
    51 K" is superseded), and 52.9–55.7 K by Clausius–Clapeyron. A loss criterion scaled by each species'
    delivery waits for a delivery budget (with T55.c).
  - **The exposed fraction f_x:** drawn once a body, log-uniform in [0.016, 0.45], on a stream this
    task chooses under the determinism rules, so that no existing value moves. The bounds are
    Ceres's 10 of 634 shadowed craters (Platz et al. 2016), the Moon's 3.5% (Li et al. 2018) and
    Mercury's 43–46% (Deutsch et al. 2016). It is labelled empirical until a delivery and gardening
    budget exists (with T55.c).
  - **What it publishes:** a `Condensates` entry
    `{ substance, Solid, reservoir, area_fraction = f_ct × f_x, seasonal: false }`, merged with
    T51.a's entry for the same substance and phase. Its reservoir is this task's to source, from
    neutron and LCROSS figures for the Moon, and is labelled a placeholder until then.
  - **T51.a's airless branch:** a condensable lies as a zonal solid only where the zonal annual
    maximum, not the mean, is below its threshold, and otherwise only in cold traps.
  - _Tests:_
    - the Moon's cold traps are 0.024–0.2% of its surface and 1.6–13% of 80–90°, with almost none
      below 70°. The bounds run from half of Williams et al. 2019's Diviner-mapped 0.048% (and its
      ~3.2% of 80–90°) to twice Hayne et al.'s point-source 0.10% (and 6.7%), since the Sun's disk
      lowers the closed form by about a fifth (R09.T7.d tests Hayne's bands at a point source);
    - its exposed water at f_x = 0.035 is within a factor of two of Li et al.'s;
    - at the temperature T49.b's curve gives for Schorghofer et al.'s 10 kg m⁻² Gyr⁻¹, half the
      Moon's CO₂ cold-trap area lies within 30–408 km². The bounds run from half of their
      peak-rate 59 km² to twice their time-averaged 204 km², over 80–90°S on 500 m Diviner pixels
      (GRL 48, e2021GL095533, Table 1). Half, since the model is symmetric and their area is the
      south's. This form is a peak-temperature one, which their comparison finds 3.5 times too small
      for CO₂ (science-r09-drainage.md §8.13). The area at the rule's own threshold is recorded,
      not asserted;
    - Ceres's permanent shadow (`cold_trap::permanent_shadow`, at Ceres's flux and angular radius,
      with Hayne et al.'s lunar terrain: 20% craters, plains σ_s 5.7°) holds Schorghofer et al.
      2024's 2,282 km² at a 4° greatest declination between craters of distribution B and A. At
      20° it is under 3% of that, 68 km², with either: their "essentially zero"
      (science-r09-drainage.md §8.10 and §8.13);
    - an airless body at 30° obliquity has none;
    - a smooth lunar pole lays no zonal cap, and a body whose zonal annual maximum is below the
      threshold everywhere lays one over its whole surface.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/cold_traps.rs`, `planetary/chem/partition.rs`;
    `crates/hyperion-surface/src/cold_trap.rs` (R09.T7.d's, read).
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::cold_traps`.
- **P14.T51.g The ice shell and its subsurface ocean** (23 → 24; after T56.d, T50.c and T49.b;
  amends T17.b, T24.b and T56.d; science-p14-subsurface-ocean.md).
  - `hooks/ocean.rs` fills T24.b's `subsurface_ocean` for every body with a solid surface, of
    every kind and origin. Its value is `Modelled<Option<SubsurfaceOcean>>`.
  - **Inputs:**
    - R and M from the bulk section;
    - the water fraction x_w: the larger of the bulk section's water fraction (for a moon, its
      own) and T51.a's condensed H₂O over M;
    - T24.a's mean surface temperature T_s;
    - T24.b's heat flow F (for a moon, with P14.T56.d's tidal heat), as Q = 4πR²F crossing the
      shell's base. Heat dissipated inside the shell would thicken it, which is recorded.
  - **The solutes** stay in the liquid, since ice Ih excludes them:
    - **Chloride:** all the body's chlorine (T50.a) as NaCl, 58.44 ÷ 35.45 of its mass.
    - **Ammonia:** for a body whose nitrogen took the icy boost (formed at or below 123 K: T50.c,
      T56.c; updated 2026-10-15), `ACCRETED_AMMONIA` = 0.0063 of its water's mass (comets' NH₃ at
      about 0.7% of H₂O by number: Mumma and Charnley 2011; Rubin et al. 2019; from memory), times
      the body's nitrogen multiple from its rank.
  - **The structure.**
    - The water is spread over the rock at 1,000 kg m⁻³ to r_w (at least 0.001 R).
    - P(r) = ρ_w G [(M − (4π/3)ρ_w R³)(1/r − 1/R) + (2π/3)ρ_w(R² − r²)].
  - **The shell** conducts Q in steady state in a sphere, with k = 651 ÷ T W m⁻¹ K⁻¹
    (`ICE_CONDUCTIVITY_COEFFICIENT`, moved here):
    - T(r) = T_s exp[Q(1/r − 1/R) ÷ (4π × 651)];
    - k is held at its 30 K value below 30 K, the law's range (Carnahan et al. 2021, checked at
      build).
  - **The liquidus:** T_L = T_m(P) − ΔT.
    - T_m is ice Ih's melting curve, IAPWS R14-08(2011), to the Ih–III–liquid triple point
      (251.165 K, 208.566 MPa).
    - ΔT sums each solute's 1-bar depression at its mass fraction in the liquid: NaCl by Bodnar
      1993, and NH₃ by a published liquidus fitted to end at T49.b's eutectic. The sum is capped
      at the largest eutectic depression present, and a solute beyond its eutectic composition
      crystallises its excess.
    - The pure and solution curves go in `substance/phase.rs`, with IAPWS's ice III, V, VI and
      VII melting curves.
  - **The ocean** is isothermal (Hammond et al. 2016). Its floor is the rock at r_w, or the
    high-pressure ice whose liquidus meets the ocean, whichever is shallower.
  - **The solve.**
    - The shell's base r_b is the unique root of T(r) − T_L(P(r), w(r)) on [r₀, R], to 1 m.
    - r₀ is the larger of r_w and the radius at 208.566 MPa.
    - w is the solutes over solutes plus the liquid down to the floor.
  - **The presence test,** `has_ocean`, closed form on the snapshot path: T(r₀) + ΔT_e ≥
    T_m(P(r₀)), ΔT_e being the largest eutectic depression present (0 with none).
  - **Published:**
    - `SubsurfaceOcean { shell_thickness, thickness, floor, liquid, solute_mass_fraction, base_temperature }`.
      The shell's thickness is also the ocean's top depth.
    - `floor` is an `OceanFloor`: `Rock`, `IceIii`, `IceV`, `IceVi` or `IceVii`.
    - `liquid` is `brine_nacl` or `nh3_h2o`, the solute whose own depression is larger, where its
      fraction is at least 10⁻³ (fresh water's 1,000 mg L⁻¹), and `H2O` otherwise.
  - **None** where T_s ≥ 273.16 K, where there is no water, or where the test fails with the
    column ending above 208.566 MPa.
  - **Not modelled (absent):**
    - where the test fails and the column reaches 208.566 MPa;
    - where the root's base lies in ice II, P_b > 14 MPa + 0.827 MPa K⁻¹ × T_b (Hammond et al.
      2016, eq. 5).
    - Both are P14.T55.k's.
  - **T56.d's branch at this bump:** an icy moon takes the ocean branch iff `has_ocean` holds at
    F_ocean, its whole heat flow with the ocean branch's tidal heat (decision-p14-moons §F-ocean
    F3), with its own water and solutes. The membrane's Λ reads this task's spherical shell
    thickness, d(F), inside T56.d's root. `has_subsurface_ocean` and
    `DerivedMoon::subsurface_ocean` go.
  - **Not produced:** the `IceShell` regime, since an ocean does not make the morphology
    (Callisto); and sulphate and methanol solutes (P14.T55.k).
  - **Held** behind `OCEAN_VERSION` = 24, with a tripwire; T54.b deletes both.
  - _Tests_ (inputs by hand; chlorine at CI's per unit rock; NH₃ at 0.0063 where the body formed
    beyond 123 K; observational figures from memory, checked at build):
    - **Europa** (1,560.8 km, 4.80 × 10²² kg, x_w 0.08, 102 K, 50 mW m⁻²): ocean under 10–16 km,
      floor `Rock`, `brine_nacl`.
    - **Ganymede** (2,634.1 km, 1.482 × 10²³ kg, 0.45, 110 K, 4.6 mW m⁻², no NH₃): under
      95–135 km, `IceV`, `brine_nacl`.
    - **Callisto** (2,410.3 km, 1.076 × 10²³ kg, 0.45, 125 K, 4.0 mW m⁻²): under 95–135 km, `IceV`,
      `nh3_h2o`.
    - **Titan** (2,574.7 km, 1.345 × 10²³ kg, 0.42, 93.7 K): under 110–150 km at 4.6 mW m⁻² and
      55–80 km at 9.9, both inside 50–200 km (Mitri et al. 2014).
    - **Enceladus** (252.1 km, 1.08 × 10²⁰ kg, 0.40, 75 K): under 20–35 km at 22 GW, floor `Rock`;
      `None` at its radiogenic heat alone.
    - **Pluto** (1,188.3 km, 1.303 × 10²² kg, 0.32, 40 K): absent at 2.45 mW m⁻²; at 3.09 an
      ocean 15–35 km thick under 270–300 km, `Rock`, `nh3_h2o`; at 3.5 one of 35–55 km under
      250–280 km (Hammond et al. 2016's warm state, 50 km under 250 km); its threshold
      2.84 ± 0.10 mW m⁻².
    - **Triton** (1,353.4 km, 2.139 × 10²² kg, 0.28, 38 K): absent at 3.28 mW m⁻²; at 4.03 an
      ocean under 225–260 km.
    - **At T24.b's heat flow:** the table's Pluto and Triton, at their rock's lag (1.26 and 1.23
      times production), hold oceans 15–35 km thick (decision-p14-moons §F-ocean F1).
    - **Ceres** (469.7 km, 9.39 × 10²⁰ kg, 0.25, 160 K, 1.24 mW m⁻², no NH₃): `None`.
    - **Rhea** (763.8 km, 2.307 × 10²¹ kg, 0.62, 76 K, 0.59 mW m⁻²): `None`.
    - **A snowball Earth** (Earth's R and M, x_w 2.3 × 10⁻⁴, 230 K, 0.087 W m⁻², chlorine at
      17 ppm): under 0.5–1.5 km.
    - **The curves:** IAPWS's triple points reproduced to 10⁻⁵, and each liquidus ending at its
      eutectic.
    - **The rule's properties:**
      - `has_ocean` equals the solve's existence of a root on 10⁴ random bodies;
      - the thickness is continuous and falls to 0 at the threshold;
      - the shell thickens as T_s or F falls;
      - without solute the base is T_m(P_b) to 10⁻⁹ K;
      - `liquid` is a registry key.
    - **T56.d's branch** reads `has_ocean`, and a moon's water fraction is its bulk section's.
    - **The hold:** below 24, every golden is unchanged, bit for bit.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/{ocean, figures, mod}.rs`, `planetary/moons/{regular, tides}.rs`,
    `planetary/system.rs`, `planetary/record.rs`, `substance/phase.rs`,
    `crates/hyperion-server/src/convert/planetary.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::ocean`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::moons`; `cargo test -p hyperion-sim substance`.
  - _Moves at 24 (estimated):_
    - every solid-surfaced body under 273.16 K gains its ocean, `None` or absence;
    - regular moons' oceans move, by the sphere, the solutes, the floor and the domain, and their
      flags flip both ways, with T56.d's branch: k₂, Im k₂, tidal heat, locking, rotation, figure,
      T24.b's heat flow, volcanism, regime, surface age and craters, and T48.a's relief;
    - captured and impact moons read their own water fraction;
    - planets' and dwarf planets' other values are unchanged;
    - goldens: `planetary/systems` with icy moons, `planetary/moons`, the protocol fixture.

- **P14.T51.h The passes' bracketed fixed point** (22 → 23; lane `p14-snapshot`, behind
  `SnapshotRules::Batch`; amends T51.b's passes; before T54.a; decision-p14-t51-batch §4).
  - The batch's passes iterate as T51.b built them, to 10⁻⁹ in T_eq, for at most 24 passes
    (the sample's slowest converging body takes 19). A body that settles keeps T51.b's bits.
  - A body not settled by then (or earlier, on a detected 2-cycle, stated) solves
    g(A) = F(A) − A, F(A) the albedo one pass at A gives, by bisection:
    - the bracket is the least and greatest albedo of its passes if g changes sign across them,
      else [0, the largest `f64` below 1], where g(0) ≥ 0 > g(1⁻) always holds;
    - 32 halvings, each one pass at the midpoint, a fixed count (2⁻³² in albedo, 10⁻⁹ in T_eq for
      A up to 0.94);
    - the published pass is the bracket's end with the smaller |g|, ties to the lower albedo.
  - `ATMOSPHERE_PASS_CAP` goes. A crate-private outcome, `Converged` or
    `Bracketed { residual }`, is kept for the tests and the bless note. A residual above 10⁻⁶ in
    albedo is a jump across the diagonal, a state or cover change with no self-consistent albedo,
    labelled and listed.
  - _Tests:_
    - converged bodies bit for bit as T51.b's (the table's three-pass bodies, so T57.a's fits are
      unmoved);
    - a stub F falling with slope −2 reaches its fixed point within 10⁻¹²;
    - a stub with a jump across the diagonal ends at the jump, its residual stated;
    - over the sample no body ends unsettled, and at most 1% is bracketed, each listed by class;
    - two runs agree to the bit.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/derive/mod.rs` and its tests.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive`, and T51.b's widened filter.

- **P14.T51.i The cold traps' fast path and their pass-invariant field** (23 → 24; lane
  `p14-snapshot`, behind `COLD_TRAPS_VERSION`; amends T51.f and, additively, rendering plan R09's
  T7.d (recorded there as R09.T7.k); before T54.b's wiring; decision-p14-t51-batch §1 and §6).
  - **One depth integral for every species** (bit for bit):
    - `hyperion_surface::cold_trap` gains a form that evaluates one latitude's shadows for several
      thresholds;
    - each population's trapezoid integrand is evaluated once on its fixed nodes, up to the
      largest cold limit;
    - each threshold's value is read from the running sums at its own limit, in
      `Population::cumulative`'s order, so it equals `fraction`'s to the bit;
    - `fraction` stays, as its one-threshold case;
    - T51.f's traps call the new form once a latitude node, for all of a body's condensables.
  - **Cheaper rules** (a value change in the surface crate; no golden reads it):
    - `instantaneous`'s Gauss–Legendre rule falls from 16 points to at most 8. GL-8 is within
      4 × 10⁻¹⁶ of 16 points, GL-6 within 7 × 10⁻¹² and GL-4 within 3 × 10⁻⁷, over colatitudes
      0.1–30°, D 0–20° and d/D 0.005–0.5. The lane states its choice and its measured difference.
    - `INTERVALS` falls from 512 to 128. The Moon's water traps move by under 3 × 10⁻⁴ of
      themselves, its CO₂ by 1.1 × 10⁻³, Mercury's by 2.6 × 10⁻⁴, and Ceres's shadow by under
      5 × 10⁻⁵. Its doc states the measured differences.
    - R09.T7.d's tests keep their tolerances, and `bowl_permanent_shadow`'s fit acceptance is
      unchanged.
  - **The albedo the cold traps read** is the regolith's Bond albedo about the body's hosts
    (T51.b's `Regolith` row: the lid's from T54.a, weathered from T54.b), not the body's area-mix
    Bond albedo.
    - The shadows lie in the regolith's craters, whose walls are the regolith (Ingersoll et al.
      1992; Hayne et al. 2021's 0.12).
    - The zonal maximum asks whether bare ground stays below the threshold.
    - The table's Moon, Mercury and Ceres move by nothing.
  - **The field.** The zonal annual maxima and each condensable's f_ct then read only the sky,
    the regolith's albedo, T24.b's heat flow and the terrain, none of which the passes change.
    So `ColdTrapField` (crate-private) is built once a body and read by every pass and by the
    record's `publish`. Its zonal entries and reservoirs stay per partition.
  - **R09.T13.f's interface stays** (decision-r09-t13f-cold-traps §3 and §8): it keeps
    `ColdTrapGround::{new, annual_maximum, fractions_at}` and `trap_threshold`, with the shared
    form inside `fractions_at`; `ColdTrapField` is built from a `ColdTrapGround`; the regolith's
    albedo is passed as `ColdTrapGroundParts::bond_albedo`. It adds
    `CondensateEntry::trapped_area_fraction` (§1.4).
  - **Budget** (release, `time_the_cold_traps`):
    - at most 0.6 ms for each qualifying table body, all its species;
    - over the 60-system sample, measured with a probe and recorded, a mean of at most 7 ms a
      system and at most 50 ms in any;
    - if missed, R09.T7.g's plains table, then main.
  - _Tests:_
    - the shared form equals `fraction` to the bit for each threshold, over the table's bodies
      and thresholds of 20–200 K;
    - T51.f's Moon, CO₂, Ceres and 30° tests hold;
    - the field is built once a body;
    - a body whose area-mix albedo rises under a zonal frost keeps the traps its regolith gives;
    - `time_the_cold_traps` prints the figures (ignored);
    - `fractions_at` through the shared form equals one `cold_trap::fraction` per threshold with
      the gate, bit for bit; `ColdTrapField`'s f_ct is the latitude integral of `fractions_at`, bit
      for bit; a merged entry's `trapped_area_fraction` is its trap's area, a zonal-only entry's 0
      and an inserted trap's its `area_fraction`; R09.T13.f's tests pass unchanged
      (decision-r09-t13f-cold-traps §7.4).
  - _Files:_ `crates/hyperion-surface/src/cold_trap.rs`; `planetary/hooks/cold_traps.rs` and its
    tests; `planetary/hooks/figures.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-surface cold_trap`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::cold_traps`; `just test-wasm-fast`.

- **P14.T51.j The oxidised surface** (23 → 24 rider; pure; after T51.c and T51.d; amends T51.d;
  decision-p14-t51-batch §5; decision-backlog-2 §1.5).
  - `hooks/modifiers.rs` (or a submodule): Bibring et al. 2006's dry, oxidising age (Science
    312, 400). A surface takes a `ferric` weathering deposit where all hold:
    - **its lid's crust (T51.c) is `basalt_fe`.** `ferric` is the oxidised `basalt_fe` alone;
      another Fe-bearing lid takes none, a closed set for the composition audit;
    - **its air is collisional at the ground and oxidising.** Collisional is P14.T51.f's test, or
      P14.T53.c's tenuous floor once it exists. Oxidising means CO₂, H₂O or O₂ present and H₂
      not the largest gas. An airless surface takes none;
    - **it is dry now** (T24.a's liquid-water flag false), and **has been for at least a
      labelled 0.1 Gyr**: since its wet epoch's end (T48.b), or over its surface age if never
      wet. A wet surface's clays and sulphates are recorded for the composition audit.
  - **Its area** is the dusty share of the dry, ice-free land: a labelled Mars value from Ruff
    and Christensen 2002's dust cover index (JGR 107, 5127), checked against Putzig et al.
    2005's bright, low-inertia terrains, both read at build. It is the same for every world until
    a dust cycle is modelled.
  - **Published** as `SurfaceModifiers::weathering_deposits` (`{ substance, area }`, at most one
    today), beside `volcanic_deposits`, and as
    `SurfaceModifiersDto.weathering_deposits: Vec<SubstanceAreaDto>`.
    - Never sent, so `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 2.
    - The client's reader takes it under T51.d's rules: each area a fraction, all deposits
      together at most 1.
  - **T54.b wires it:**
    - a palette `Deposit` entry `ferric`, the source of the body's sand and dust;
    - its area in the area mix, at `ferric`'s optics (P14.T49.i).

    `mars_dust` stays R09's reference worlds' row and R08's aerosol; no generated palette places
    it.

  - **Also in its commit** (test only): T51.d's Mercury test reads
    - k above 1, both terms printed;
    - its dust term within 10.5–17.5 (Cintala 1992's "almost 14 times" ± 25%);
    - its wind term's open share within 0.4–0.6.

    The `k ÷ 4 ∈ [1, 3)` pin goes (decision-p14-t51-batch §3).

  - _Tests:_
    - a Mars (T51.c's `basalt_fe` lid, its measured CO₂ given by hand, dry for 3.5 Gyr) carries
      the deposit over the share of its ice-free land;
    - the same body under liquid water carries none;
    - an airless `basalt_fe` body, a `basalt` lid, an H₂-dominated air, and a world dry for under
      0.1 Gyr each carry none;
    - deterministic, with no draw, and no existing value moves.
  - _Sources:_ Bibring et al. 2006; Ruff and Christensen 2002; Putzig et al. 2005; Hu, Ehlmann
    and Seager 2012 (the row's spectral type).
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/modifiers.rs`; the protocol's surface-modifiers DTO; the client's
    reader.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::modifiers`; `just gen-protocol-check`.

#### P14.T52 Atmospheric chemistry

Surface path, `planetary/chem/`. Built only with a `surface` or `envelope` section, and never
feeding back into p_s, T_s, the albedo or the bulk.

- **P14.T52.a Equilibrium speciation, hydrogen-dominated** (23 → 24, updated 2026-10-15; after
  T49.d and T50.b).
  - `chem/equilibrium.rs`: at the 1-bar level, the quench level and the photosphere of an envelope
    (or a thin H₂ air once T53.a keeps one), Heng and Tsai 2016's analytic C–H–O–N solution
    ("accurate at the ∼1% level for temperatures from 500 to 3000 K", gas phase), on T49.d's K(T),
    with:
    - H₂S carrying the sulphur (Visscher, Lodders and Fegley 2006);
    - the trace elements (Na, K, Ti, V, Fe, Mg, Si, Ca, Al, P, Cl, Cr, Mn, Ni, Zn) in closed form
      from the major solution, each metal as its neutral atom and its first ion. Second ions are
      under 10⁻³ of the first below 5,000 K, and H⁺ is under 10⁻⁶ of H, so neither is carried. The
      builder states every species it lists, each a T49.b row
      (science-r08-unowned-absorbers);
    - e⁻ and H⁻ by Saha's closed form, the charge balanced over the metals' first ions. Above
      Heng and Tsai's 3,000 K, the closed form is extended to atoms and ions (T52.b's
      dissociation), and the extension is recorded.
  - Below 500 K the major carriers are all-in, and the composition is the quench level's.
  - A fixed-count Newton refinement on the five element potentials from the analytic start is
    added only if the asserted values below fail the stated tolerance, and is recorded.
  - T50.b's E is fitted from 14.5 to 318 M⊕. Below about 5 M⊕ an envelope's metals exceed 0.2 per
    H atom, so the builder states where Heng and Tsai's solution stops and what the record says
    beyond it (decision-p14-t50b-envelope §5).
  - The solution accepts C/O above 1 (between the CO₂ and CO lines, about hosts above 0.545).
  - **Validation:** values computed by hand with FastChem or GGchem (both GPL-3.0) outside the
    repository, asserted only, each with the code's version, its inputs and its command in the
    test's doc comment. Neither code is vendored, linked, ported or run by any recipe
    (decision-composition §5).
  - _Tests:_
    - CH₄ = CO and NH₃ = N₂ at Lodders and Fegley 2002's boundaries (from memory) within a stated
      tolerance;
    - H₂S the dominant sulphur gas;
    - Fe monatomic above the iron cloud (Visscher et al. 2010);
    - element conservation at 10⁻¹²;
    - the charge balances to 10⁻¹², and each metal's atom and ion sum to its abundance to 10⁻¹²;
    - every asserted case within tolerance;
    - bit-identical natively and under `wasm32-wasip1` (the sim's slow wasip1 suite).
  - _Files:_ `planetary/chem/equilibrium.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::equilibrium`.
- **P14.T52.b Quench and photochemical rules** (23 → 24, updated 2026-10-15).
  - `chem/{quench, photochem}.rs`:
    - Zahnle and Marley 2014's quench relations for CO, CH₄, NH₃, HCN and CO₂, with a stated
      K_zz law ("If vertical mixing is like Jupiter's, the transition from methane to CO occurs at
      500 K in a planet"; 400–600 K by mixing);
    - rules, each with its source and range:
      - photochemical SO₂ from H₂S on warm giants (Tsai et al. 2023);
      - S₈ haze at 250–700 K (Gao et al. 2017);
      - hydrocarbon (soot) haze below 950 K, and silicates above (Gao et al. 2020);
      - the ice giants' haze above their CH₄ layer (Irwin et al. 2022);
      - the cold giants' chromophore no deeper than about 0.2 bar (Braude et al. 2020);
      - thermal dissociation of H₂O, TiO and VO on ultra-hot daysides (Parmentier et al. 2018;
        Lothringer, Barman and Koskinen 2018).
  - T24.c's ozone and methane-haze rules stay T24.c's. A desiccated world's CO + O₂ is T53.a's
    (snapshot path).
  - _Tests:_
    - Jupiter's CO above its equilibrium value at 1 bar, by the quench;
    - the CH₄ → CO transition near 500 K for Jupiter-like mixing;
    - S₈ haze only at 250–700 K;
    - soot only below 950 K;
    - each rule continuous in its inputs.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/chem/{quench, photochem}.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::quench`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::photochem`.
- **P14.T52.c Condensation aloft over the registry** (23 → 24, updated 2026-10-15; after T49.b
  and T49.e).
  - `chem/condense.rs`: for each row with a law aloft whose limiting element is present and whose
    range meets the profile:
    - its base where the vapour reaches saturation along T24.e's T(p) or the envelope's profile,
      by a fixed count of Newton steps;
    - cold traps hottest base first, with ties by `SubstanceId`, each removing its limiting element
      above its base (Spiegel, Silverio and Burrows 2009);
    - the column and the mixing ratio above by Ackerman and Marley 2001's f_sed;
    - modes with material, deck, size distribution, column mass, and τ(550) from T49.e;
    - coverage scaled to the snapshot path's cloud fraction.
  - T24.c's deck rule, T24.d's NH₃, NH₄SH and H₂O decks and T24.g's H₂SO₄ are rows of this loop.
  - _Tests:_
    - Jupiter's NH₃ deck at 0.5–1 bar;
    - Uranus's CH₄ layer at 1–2 bar and an H₂S layer below 5 bar (Irwin et al. 2022);
    - a 1,200 K giant's silicate and iron decks below its photosphere, and none of NH₃ or H₂O;
    - KCl and ZnS on a 600 K sub-Neptune at high metallicity (Morley et al. 2013);
    - TiO cold-trapped where CaTiO₃ forms below it;
    - Venus's H₂SO₄ deck as T24.g's tests;
    - each base on its saturation curve to 10⁻⁶ in pressure;
    - the limiting element conserved through the traps.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/chem/condense.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::condense`.
- **P14.T52.d Envelopes across temperature** (23 → 24, updated 2026-10-15; with T24.d, last of
  its lane).
  - `hooks/envelope_atmosphere.rs`, T24.d's structure, with:
    - T50.b's abundances, speciated by T52.a and quenched and photolysed by T52.b;
    - decks by T52.c;
    - hazes by T52.b;
    - every atom and first ion of T52.a's metals (Na, K, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Ni,
      Zn), with TiO, VO, FeH, SiO, H, H⁻ and e⁻, where T52.a puts them, each with its column and
      layer, for R08.T4.e's lines (science-r08-unowned-absorbers).
  - _Tests:_
    - Sudarsky et al. 2000's five classes in their ranges: NH₃ clouds below about 150 K, water
      near 250 K, clear above about 350 K, alkalis at 900–1,500 K, silicates above about 1,500 K
      or at low gravity (their abstract, verified by the atmospheres audit; T24.d's draft had
      1,400 K from memory);
    - Fortney et al. 2008's pM/pL split by TiO;
    - water and TiO dissociated on a KELT-9b-like dayside (Kitzmann et al. 2018; Lothringer et
      al. 2018);
    - a KELT-9b-like dayside lists Fe⁺ above Fe and Ca⁺ above Ca, and every T50.b metal's atom;
    - Jupiter's T24.d tests kept (T(1 bar) 166 K ± 10%, NH₃ deck at 0.5–1 bar, CH₄/H₂ about
      2 × 10⁻³);
    - a sub-Neptune's envelope `Ok`;
    - continuous in time, but at recorded state changes.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/{envelope_atmosphere, mod}.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::envelope_atmosphere`.

#### P14.T53 Escape, special states and life

- **P14.T53.a Escape by regime and fractionation** (23 → 24; amends T13.b).
  - `chem/escape.rs`, on the snapshot path, over T13.b's fluence:
    - Jeans as built;
    - a non-thermal and impact term set by the cosmic shoreline (Zahnle and Catling 2017: I ∝
      v_esc⁴, impact erosion at v_imp ≈ 4–5 v_esc), calibrated so that the table's Mars keeps 3–10
      mbar of CO₂ and loses its 0.11 bar of N₂ (ruling 119.4 superseded, by this bump) and Titan
      keeps its N₂;
    - diffusion-limited hydrogen escape with fractionation (Hunten 1973; Zahnle and Kasting 1986;
      both from memory), leaving helium in envelopes (Hu, Seager and Yung 2015; Malsky et
      al. 2023), oxygen on water-losing worlds (Luger and Barnes 2015), and methane as a minor gas
      through nitrogen, at most at its diffusion limit, with carbon's outcome, escape against
      photolysis to hydrocarbons, recorded (science-p14-t24f §4). It replaces T24.f's single O₂
      route, including its young-melt uptake, which becomes Schaefer et al. 2016's FeO → FeO₁.₅
      exchange integrated over the loss, with the greenhouse's melt timed; and it takes up the
      oxygen of temperate worlds whose cold trap fails for want of a non-condensing background
      (Wordsworth and Pierrehumbert 2014; science-p14-t24f §3);
    - a desiccated CO₂ world under an M dwarf turning about 40% of its CO₂ into CO and O₂ once its
      H falls below 1 ppm (Gao et al. 2015);
    - the H₂ and He below `THIN_ENVELOPE_FRACTION` kept as air, with an H₂ collision-induced
      greenhouse term calibrated on Pierrehumbert and Gaidos 2011 and Wordsworth and
      Pierrehumbert 2013 (the latter from memory);
    - each element's outcome recorded;
    - each envelope's He/H after fractionation, stated, which T54.b passes to T50.b as its
      primordial He/H (decision-p14-t50b-envelope §5);
    - the CO₂ term's form: once Mars holds its 3–10 mbar of CO₂, the grey √p form puts it at about
      241 K against its measured ~210 K (decision-p14-moons, item 4). This subtask chooses a form
      that holds the measured Venus, Earth and Mars together, and refits every greenhouse constant
      on a measured state (P14.T57.a's rule). Mars's surface temperature joins its tests, within
      T13.c's 8%.
  - _Tests:_
    - Mars as above;
    - Titan keeps N₂, and keeps its methane reservoir over 4.57 Gyr at its median carbon;
    - a planet of a dimming M dwarf whose mantle freezes during its runaway keeps only the oxygen
      freed after it froze;
    - TRAPPIST-1 b and c, LHS 3844 b and Mercury airless or under 1 mbar (Greene et al. 2023;
      Zieba et al. 2023; Kreidberg et al. 2019);
    - a 5 M⊕ core stripped at 0.05 au as today;
    - a 2 R⊕ planet near the valley's upper edge reaching a helium mass fraction above 0.4 in some
      draws (Malsky et al. 2023);
    - escape continuous and monotone in time.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/chem/escape.rs`, `planetary/derive/atmosphere.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::escape`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive::atmosphere`.
- **P14.T53.b The steam envelope** (23 → 24; amends T13.c).
  - A runaway world loses water only up to its diffusion- or energy-limited capacity over its
    history (Luger and Barnes 2015). The rest stays:
    - steam over a surface where the column allows one;
    - `SteamEnvelope` where the water lies above its critical point (647.1 K, 22.06 MPa) with no
      interface.
  - This subtask decides which section a `SteamEnvelope` body fills (lean: the `envelope` section,
    surface `NotApplicable`, with `has_solid_surface` read from the state, recorded against
    decision-p14-t35e-wire's equivalence), and its albedo and cloud.
  - _Tests:_
    - a 25%-water world inside the runaway limit is `SteamEnvelope`;
    - an Earth-water world loses its oceans as today;
    - Venus unchanged.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/derive/atmosphere.rs`, `planetary/record.rs` (read), `planetary/chem/escape.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive::atmosphere`.
- **P14.T53.c Thin and transient air** (23 → 24; after T51.a, T51.b and T53.a; amends T13.b for
  ice-held volatiles; decision-triton-and-e101 §1.8).
  - `chem/tenuous.rs`: `Tenuous` between a stated floor and the 100 Pa line, where a gas is held:
    - **An ice-held volatile's retention.** A condensable whose partition (T51.a) holds most of
      its inventory as surface ice, its saturation pressure at its ice's temperature below its
      inventory's weight, is not judged by `Retention::of`'s threshold. That threshold is T13.b's
      calibrated classifier of whether a bulk air survives, and is not a flux. Such a condensable
      keeps its inventory less its loss over the system's age, the escape of its own
      vapour-pressure air integrated over the age (Schaller and Brown 2007, ApJ 659, L61;
      Johnson et al. 2015, ApJ 809, 43; Zahnle and Catling 2017, ApJ 843, 122, §2.1). The escape
      is taken at the cold upper atmosphere such airs have, 1.7–2.7 times the ice's temperature
      (Pluto's 65–68 K at about 2,900 km, Young et al. 2018, Icarus 300, 174; Triton's 102 K at
      870 km), within T53.a's regimes.
      - The loss law is stated and cited. Pluto's measured escape is its check within a factor
        of 10: 1 × 10²³ N₂ and 5 × 10²⁵ CH₄ s⁻¹ (Gladstone et al. 2016, Science 351, aad8866).
        Pluto's energy-limited rate expected before the flyby, 0.7–4 × 10²⁷ s⁻¹, would empty the
        model's median Pluto.
      - Methane keeps following nitrogen (P14.T24.f). A species held airborne keeps T13.b's
        verdict, so Titan's, Ganymede's and Callisto's N₂ do not move: N₂'s saturation pressure
        at their 94 and 110 K surfaces is 5 and 14 bar.
    - **The ice's temperature.** An ice-held dominant condensable's controlling temperature
      (T51.a's coldest zone) is its ice's own.
      - It is one temperature over all of its ice, which latent heat keeps uniform (Gladstone et
        al. 2016; Young, Braga-Ribas and Johnson 2020, Fig. 5).
      - It comes from the energy balance of the ice's area, at the ice's albedo (T49.c, T51.b) and
        a stated, cited emissivity (Triton's 0.59 ± 0.16, Hillier et al. 1990, Science 250,
        419), not the bare surface's 0.95.
      - Its pressure is the registry's saturation pressure there: on β-N₂, 1.4 Pa at 37.25 K.
    - The sublimation air from T51.a's partition (Pluto, Triton), its gases listed, and its haze
      by T24.c's methane rule where CH₄ is present.
    - Io's patchy SO₂ air from T24.g's outgassing under `Extreme` volcanism.
  - Exospheres are P14.T55.c's, and seasonal transport and frost by month P14.T55.e's.
  - The docs of `JEANS_RETENTION_THRESHOLD`, `Retention` and `AIRLESS_PRESSURE` name the
    verdict's scope, a bulk air's, and this ice-held case.
  - _Tests:_
    - the table's Triton at its distance and own bulk is `Tenuous`, its N₂ within a factor of 3
      of 1.4 Pa and its ice within 2 K of 38 ± 1 K (moved from T51.b). The 1.4 Pa is Voyager 2's
      14 ± 2 µbar (Gurrola 1995, as Marques Oliveira et al. 2022, A&A 659, A136, quote it),
      14.1 ± 0.4 µbar in 2017 (Marques Oliveira et al.) and 14.5 ± 0.5 µbar in 2022 (Sicardy et
      al. 2024, arXiv:2402.02476); the 38 ± 1 K is Tryka et al. 1994, Icarus 112, 513;
    - a Pluto at its inventory carries N₂ with CH₄ and a haze (Gladstone et al. 2016), its N₂
      within a factor of 10 of 1.1 Pa: 11 ± 1 and 10 ± 1 µbar in 2015, 12.2 µbar in 2020 (Sicardy
      et al. 2021, arXiv:2112.07764). The band is wider than Triton's because its measured season
      is not its orbit mean;
    - a Charon at Pluto's distance keeps no N₂, while Pluto and Triton keep theirs (Johnson et
      al. 2015);
    - the table's Titan, Ganymede and Callisto keep T13.b's N₂ verdicts;
    - the table's Ganymede and Callisto stay `Airless`. Their radiogenic argon (Ganymede's 15 Pa
      at 23) is not an air; their real airs are exospheres (P14.T55.c). T53.a's non-thermal term
      or this subtask's floor settles it, or the builder records it for "main";
    - the record says `Tenuous`, not `Airless`, where a gas is held above the floor;
    - every `Airless` body has an empty gas list.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/chem/tenuous.rs`, `planetary/derive/atmosphere.rs`,
    `planetary/chem/partition.rs` (the controlling temperature).
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::chem::tenuous`;
    `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::derive::atmosphere`.
- **P14.T53.d The biosphere hook** (23 → 24).
  - `hooks/biosphere.rs`: `Biosphere { fluxes: Vec<(SubstanceId, f64)> }`, the net surface fluxes
    of O₂, CH₄ and N₂O in units of Earth's present biotic flux of each, and the palette's `Cover`
    role with a `biological` flag. `NotModelled` until a life plan exists: no rule here makes
    life.
  - When fluxes are given, the chemistry treats them as sources: O₂'s steady state against its
    sinks, O₃ from O₂ by T24.c's rule, and CH₄'s lifetime in an oxic air.
  - _Tests:_
    - every generated body is abiotic, with its member absent;
    - the table's Earth, given Earth's fluxes by hand, reaches 0.21 bar of O₂ within a factor of 2
      and an ozone column within a factor of 2 of 300 DU;
    - fluxes with no sinks stated are refused.
  - _Files:_ `planetary/hooks/biosphere.rs`.
  - _Accept:_ `cargo test -p hyperion-sim planetary::hooks::biosphere`.

#### P14.T54 The composition batches on the record

- **P14.T54.a The 22 → 23 batch on the record, and its bump.** It is the last of the 22 → 23
  batch, "the surface": the snapshot path and the surface members, everything R09's `for_body`
  reads (decision-bump-plan-after-22, 2026-10-14; re-cut, updated 2026-10-15).
  - `record::Surface` fills `condensates` (T51.a) and `crust` (T51.c), and `surface_liquids` and
    `surface_ices` gain T51.a's entries. `vertical_structure`, `aerosols` and `record::Envelope`
    stay `NotModelled` until T54.b.
  - T24.a's `SurfaceInputs` takes the lid's regolith inertia, P14.T49.j's
    `reference_regolith_thermal_inertia` at T51.c's lid, in place of `SurfaceMaterial`
    (decision-p14-t49c-split §1.3). That retires `ROCK_REGOLITH_THERMAL_INERTIA_J_PER_M2_K_SQRT_S`
    and `ICE_REGOLITH_THERMAL_INERTIA_J_PER_M2_K_SQRT_S` (science-p14-t24a-climate.md §6, item 2).
    The bless note accounts for the airless nights it moves.
  - T13's passes call T51.a and T51.b, and T57.a's constants take effect. T49.b's fitted curves
    replace the five Clausius–Clapeyron sets, and its c_p(T) replaces `HeatCapacityClass`.
    `registry.golden`'s gas columns and `substances.json` (`heat_capacity_over_r_298k`; the
    `absorber` flags T49.b's rows hold off until this bump: H₂'s, He's, N₂'s and CO₂'s, and the
    fifteen rows R08.T19 owes answers, once answered (Risks, "Deviations in P14.T49.b, as built"))
    are re-blessed.
  - `MOONS_VERSION` and its tripwire are deleted (T56.a, T56.c, T56.d), so that the moons' Laplace
    planes, own ranks and tides, and the rings' normals, take effect with the batch. The bless note
    accounts for them by subtask.
  - The server's conversion sends every ring's `normal`. Its `MOONS_VERSION` test goes, and
    `a_ring_s_normal_is_sent_from_the_batch_s_bump` becomes a test that every golden ring carries
    `Ring::normal()`. `scene_systems.golden` gains the field. The shared fixture's ring
    (`packages/protocol/fixtures/planetary.json`) gains a unit normal on its planet's pole's side,
    and the client's tests build the absent case by removing it. The field stays optional on the
    wire, for older servers (decision-p14-t56a §1).
