    `rng/tags.rs`, `planetary/mod.rs`, and R09's `hyperion-surface/src/cold_trap.rs`, whose
    `flux_weighted_elevation` is made public, additively, with a doc, an example and a test that
    it is the elevation `fraction` reads, so that the zonal annual maximum takes the same star.
    `partition.rs`'s `sublimation_edge` is `pub(crate)` with its loss rate a parameter (the same
    bits at 144 kg m⁻² Gyr⁻¹), with `exosphere_threshold`, `SolidEdges` and `publish_with` (whose
    `Partition` arm is `publish` to the bit, the partition golden unmoved), and
    `Condensates::with_cold_traps` with `TrappedIce`. The draw sits in `hooks/cold_traps.rs`, not
    beside `continental_asymptote`; the grain density is read in `partition.rs`, already behind
    its hold in the optics tripwire, so the tripwire's `HELD` list is unchanged.
  - _The collisional test:_ a body takes the cold traps where it is airless and its column holds
    fewer than 1 ÷ σ_c molecules per square metre, p < m̄ g ÷ σ_c, with σ_c 3 × 10⁻¹⁹ m² (a
    hard-sphere N₂/O cross-section, _from memory_, 28% below N₂'s 4.16 × 10⁻¹⁹ m²; deferred
    findings) and m̄ its column's mean molecular mass, or N₂'s
    where it is empty: 2.5 × 10⁻⁷ Pa on the Moon. Pluto and Triton (about 1 Pa) are collisional
    and keep P14.T51.a's edges; at 23 their N₂ is deleted, so they qualify until P14.T53.c gives
    them their airs. On the table, Mercury, the Moon and Ceres qualify, and Ganymede (14.8 Pa)
    does not. A body locked 1:1 to its star (the `Eyeball` profile) takes none.
  - _The airless branch at 24_ (`SolidEdges::Exosphere`): every solid's edge is its threshold,
    its net Hertz–Knudsen edge into vacuum at 144 kg m⁻² Gyr⁻¹ (its pure row's, below its first
    melt), against the zonal annual maximum; its mass is what its zonal area holds at 1.93 km, at
    most its reservoir, so that the rest is left for its traps (P14.T51.a gave a solid-lying
    reservoir whole to its entry). Water takes the same rule with the partition's condensed water
    and the registry's threshold (110.0 K, within 1 K of `AIRLESS_ICE_TEMPERATURE`), but on an
    ice-rich crust, which keeps P14.T24.b's ice and takes no water traps. The zonal annual maximum
    is flat ground in equilibrium with the star at its highest, σT⁴ = ((1 − A) S_p sin e + q) ÷ ε at
    the annual-mean profile's 66 area points: the Moon's pole 158.13 K and 85° 226.87 K (A 0.11,
    q 0.0119 W m⁻²), Mercury's pole 172.07 K with the disk and 110.27 K as a point, and a rocky
    equator at 12.3 au 110.41 K.
  - _The latitude rule:_ four-point Gauss–Legendre on 0, 60, 70, 80, 85, 88 and 90°, 24 nodes,
    against a 0.02° midpoint rule over 60–90°: −3.99 × 10⁻⁴ for craters of distribution B and
    +1.07 × 10⁻⁴ for A (the test's bound is 5 × 10⁻⁴). Nodes whose zonal annual maximum is below
    the threshold take no trap.
  - _The figures as built_ (the real Sun at Earth's perihelion, the Sun's 0.2711°, δ 1.54°, A
    0.12, q 0.018 W m⁻², 20% craters, plains at RMS slope 0.1, the 0.05 cut-off): the Moon's water
    traps 0.0922% of its surface and 5.838% of 80–90° with B, 0.0595% and 3.867% with A, none
    below 70°; its exposed water at f_x 0.035 is 1,224 km² with B (×1.91 of 3.5% of Diviner's
    18,300 km², ×0.87 of the all-scale 40,000 km²) and 789 km² with A (×1.23, ×0.56); half its CO₂
    traps at 10 kg m⁻² Gyr⁻¹ (55.53 K on T49.b's curve) 194 km² with B and 187 km² with A, and at
    the rule's own threshold, 58.18 K (not the research's estimated 57 K), 364 and 342 km²,
    recorded, not asserted; Ceres's permanent shadow at 4° 1,049 km² with B and 7,557 km² with A,
    about Schorghofer et al. 2024's 2,282 km², and at 20° 0 and 52.7 km²; at 30° no water or CO₂
    traps.
  - _The terrain stand-ins_, each labelled: a crater fraction of 0.2 × min(1, N(>100 m) ÷ Trask's
    saturation at 100 m), Hayne et al. 2021's lunar best fit with the lane's 100 m reference; d/D
    Hayne et al.'s distribution B, the one that passes every band test (science-r09-drainage.md
    §8.13.3); plains at atan 0.1 (5.7°); and the lunar share under the conduction cut-off, 0.05,
    for every body, until a crater state and a regolith give their own.
  - _The reservoir placeholder:_ water's column over its trap area is 22.5 kg m⁻² (Lunar
    Prospector's about 1.5 wt% if confined to the shadows, Feldman et al. 2001, _from memory_, over
    1 m at 1,500 kg m⁻³; LCROSS's 5.6 ± 2.9 wt%, about 84 kg m⁻², the upper check), CO₂'s LCROSS's
    2.17% of water by number (Colaprete et al. 2010, Table 1, _from memory_) × 44.01 ÷ 18.02, 1.19
    kg m⁻², and a species of the inventory takes what is left after its zonal deposit, at most
    water's column over its own trap area. A merged entry adds the trap's area and reservoir to
    the zonal entry, keeps its seasonal flag, and sums the two layers, the trap's at its grain
    density at its threshold. The angular radius is the brightest zone star's, and the flux the
    body's orbit-mean flux from every host taken to periapsis as its seasonal host's.
  - _The cost_ (`time_the_cold_traps`, in release, under the heavy lock at a 100% CPU quota, the
    1-minute load 4.7): about 3.1 ms a qualifying body of the table, for its two species (Mercury
    3.21 ms, the Moon 3.05 ms, Ceres 3.06 ms), against P14.T51.a's 0.17 ms, so about 1.5 ms a
    species where the research estimated 0.5–0.8 ms; the bodies that do not qualify move by under
    0.01 ms.
  - _The passes_ (**owned by P14.T54.b, over P14.T51.i's field**, which makes one evaluation a body
    serve every pass, decision-p14-t51-batch §6) (`surface_mix::pass_condensates`) keep P14.T51.a's
    airless branch. From 24 the
    record takes the cold traps' branch, so P14.T54.b must give T13.c's passes the same sky and
    rules, or the Bond albedo reads other areas than the record publishes. The cold traps'
    tripwire names it among what T54.b settles.
  - _The batch review's fixes_ (2026-10-19; no value moves): `Sunlit::annual_maximum` takes its
    colatitude as `Radians` and `trap_reservoir` returns `KilogramsPerSquareMetre`;
    `flux_weighted_elevation`'s example compares bits and its doc states its domain (a centre
    below −α, a disk wholly set, gives NaN); the latitude rule's docs say "within 5 × 10⁻⁴", the
    test's bound; carbon dioxide's threshold is stated as the registry's 58.18 K at 144 kg m⁻²
    Gyr⁻¹; the regolith's 1,500 kg m⁻³ is labelled _from memory_; and σ_c's doc records N₂'s
    kinetic diameter.
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)**, from P14.T51.f:
  - _The cost per system_ (**ruled: P14.T51.i's fast path and field**, decision-p14-t51-batch §1;
    measured after it at 0.50 ms a qualifying table body and a mean of 0.83 ms a system, P14.T51.i's
    record) (for main, before P14.T54.b): about 3.1 ms for each airless body that is
    not locked to its star and whose air is not collisional, for its two delivered species (about
    1.5 ms more for each further condensable), against P14.T33.a's 3.47 ms a field system and
    decision-p14-t51a-partition §6's refusal of 2.1 ms a body. Over the 60-system sample under the
    batch's rules (the derived planets, members and moons, 2026-10-19, a probe run once by name
    and not kept): 688 such bodies, 170 of them moons, with 94 more locked to their star and so
    taking none; a mean of 11.5 a system (median 8, at most 73), so about 36 ms a system (median
    25 ms, at most 0.23 s), some ten times a field system's whole cost. At 23's stand-ins a
    Pluto's or a Triton's N₂ is deleted, so they count until P14.T53.c.
  - _Grazing-angle albedo_ (**ruled deferred**, not made before 24, decision-p14-t51-batch §2: for
    P14.T55.c's rough-ground zonal annual maximum) (for main): Hayne et al. 2017 (JGR Planets 122,
    2371, eq. A8 and Table
    A1) give A(θ) = A₀ + 0.06 (θ ÷ 45°)³ + 0.25 (θ ÷ 90°)⁸ at the solar incidence angle θ. With it
    the Moon's polar T_max falls from 158 to 111 K, its 85° from 227 to 182 K, and Mercury's pole
    from 172 to 118 K. The current results survive, but the lunar pole's margin to water's 110 K
    drops to 1 K. It is an algorithm change, so it is not made here.
  - _Bodies locked to their star_ keep P14.T51.a's blended edge, so P14.T51.a's "_For
    P14.T51.f._" item (a condensable alone in an exosphere takes the under-air edge) stays open
    for them.
  - _σ_c_ is 28% below N₂'s hard-sphere cross-section: N₂'s kinetic diameter is 364 pm (Ismail et
    al. 2015, through a secondary), so π d² = 4.16 × 10⁻¹⁹ m² against the code's 3 × 10⁻¹⁹ m²,
    kept.
  - _Mercury's larger reservoir:_ its polar deposits are far larger than the Moon's (Lawrence et
    al. 2013, _from memory_), against the lunar 22.5 kg m⁻² that every body takes until a delivery
    and gardening budget exists (with P14.T55.c).
  - _T_max at equilibrium_ with the star at its highest overstates the peak on a fast rotator of
    high thermal inertia, where the ground does not reach equilibrium within a day.
  - _The peak-temperature form_ understates the most volatile species' traps: Schorghofer et al.
    2021 find about 3.5 times the CO₂ area by the time-averaged loss (science-r09-drainage.md
    §8.13).
  - _The model is symmetric_ about the equator, where the Moon's south holds about 60% of its
    traps (Hayne et al. 2021).
  - _The present obliquity_ stands for its history, which the cold traps record (Ceres's 2–20°
    cycle; science-r09-drainage.md §4.3 item 7).
  - _Delivered species lie only in traps:_ water and CO₂ with no inventory take their
    placeholder columns over their traps and no zonal deposit.
  - _Locked bodies and collisional thin airs take none:_ a body locked 1:1 to its star has no
    star circling its sky, and an air at or above m̄ g ÷ σ_c (Pluto, Triton, Ganymede's 14.8 Pa on
    the table) keeps P14.T51.a's blended edges against the annual mean.
  - _SO₂, H₂S and CO_ have phase diagrams but no gas columns, so no inventory holds them and they
    take no traps: a closed set, for the composition audit.
- **Deviations in P14.T51.h, as built (`p14-t51hij`, 2026-10-19).** The passes' bracketed fixed
  point, behind the `p14-snapshot` lane's hold (`SnapshotRules::Batch`, `SNAPSHOT_VERSION` = 23):
  under `Held`, in force at 22, nothing moves and no golden reads it. The ruling is
  decision-p14-t51-batch §4.
  - _Where it is._ The solver is a module of its own, `planetary/derive/passes.rs` (crate-private,
    generic over the pass, so that its stubs test it), which `PassBody::passes` calls under `Batch`;
    `planetary/derive/mod.rs` keeps the held arm, T13.c's three, as it was, and drives the batch's
    passes through `PassDriver` (`derive_body_driven`; `derive_body_under` drives `Solve`), whose
    test-only `T51b` arm is P14.T51.b's loop as it was built, for the bit-for-bit test. Files beyond
    the plan's:
    `derive/atmosphere.rs` and `atmosphere/surface_mix.rs` (`LARGEST_BOND_ALBEDO`, the clamp,
    re-exported for the bracket's upper bound), `moons/regular.rs` (the test getters) and
    `system/tests.rs` (the sample test).
  - _The constants:_ `PLAIN_PASSES` 24, `HALVINGS` 32 and `JUMP_RESIDUAL` 10⁻⁶;
    `ATMOSPHERE_PASS_CAP` is deleted. A body takes at most 24 + 32 + 1 = 57 passes: the one more
    where a bound of [0, 1⁻] is still an end of the bracket after the halvings, so its g is taken
    for the choice of end (the ruling's "at most 56" omits it). The midpoint is `f64::midpoint`, and
    a halving whose midpoint is not strictly inside the bracket stops the halvings, which moves
    nothing, since that pass is an end's.
  - _The outcome_ (`passes::Convergence`, crate-private, on `DerivedBody::convergence` with a test
    getter on `DerivedMoon`): `Converged`, `Bracketed { residual }`, and **`Fixed`, a third
    variant** for the held rules' three passes, which neither converge nor bracket (a deviation from
    the ruling's two, so that a held body is not called converged). `is_jump` marks a residual above
    `JUMP_RESIDUAL`.
  - _The bracket's signs:_ the bisection keeps the lower end's side of the diagonal, g ≥ 0 taken as
    one side, so that a bracket from the passes in either orientation halves soundly. The bound
    1⁻ is taken as g < 0 without a pass; where F(1⁻) = 1⁻ (a lossless frost at the area mix's
    clamp) g is 0 there, and the bound, kept as an end, is taken and published at a residual of 0.
  - _The detected 2-cycle (stated):_ the plain passes stop where the albedo a pass reads equals, by
    `total_cmp`, the one read two passes before. A pass is a function of the albedo it reads alone
    (the passes' surface is built once before the first), so the passes would repeat the cycle,
    and the least and greatest albedos read and g at each are those 24 plain passes end with: the
    published pass is the same to the bit, tested against the passes run on
    (`stopping_at_a_detected_2_cycle_moves_nothing`). It saves passes only.
  - _Bit for bit:_ `atmosphere::tests::a_body_that_settles_keeps_t51b_s_bits` derives every body of
    the table, Jupiter, an icy member as recorded and as placed, and a Pluto under both drivers and
    holds every field equal, the count and the outcome included (the table's three-pass bodies, so
    T57.a's fits do not move); `passes::tests::on_stubs_the_solver_settles_as_t51b_s_loop` holds
    the solver to the loop on 361 linear stubs. Checked once over the sample (a probe, not kept):
    every one of the 934
    converged bodies took the same passes as at T51.b, and 933 compared to the bit in the albedo,
    T_eq and T_s against T51.b's loop restored (the 934th, a three-pass body, was dropped by the
    probe's filter); the table's lines too.
  - _The slope test:_ "a stub F falling with slope −2 reaches its fixed point within 10⁻¹²" is met
    by a stub held into a band about its fixed point (10⁻³ below, 1.5 × 10⁻³ above, as a cloud's
    availability is held at 1), whose passes 2-cycle at the band's edges: 2.3 × 10⁻¹³ from the
    fixed point. Unbounded, the slope drives the passes to the clamps, and 32 halvings of a bracket
    0.75 wide reach only 1.75 × 10⁻¹⁰ (tested at 2⁻³²); 10⁻¹² there would need 39.
  - _The sample_ (the first 60 systems generated whole, 954 bodies, 2026-10-19): passes
    {3: 764, 4: 100, 5: 12, 6: 14, 7: 12, 8: 2, 9: 1, 10: 3, 11: 4, 12: 1, 13: 2, 14: 2, 15: 3,
    16: 6, 17: 5, 18: 2, 19: 1, 36: 5, 37: 8, 38: 2, 40: 2, 56: 3}. 934 converge as at T51.b, and
    the 20 at T51.b's cap are bracketed, 2.1%, in three classes:
    - **5 fixed points the plain passes oscillate about**, the temperate rocky worlds (residuals
      1.0 × 10⁻¹²–4.2 × 10⁻¹¹, all under 10⁻⁹, asserted): each publishes its self-consistent albedo,
      0.197–0.276 (T_eq 216–249 K, T_s 272–280 K), in place of whichever end of its 2-cycle the cap's
      parity landed on. T51.h owns them, and they are settled.
    - **8 lossless visible-only frosts at the clamp**, airless icy members and one rocky member,
      each published at the area mix's clamp, 1⁻, a fixed point there (residual 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁶), with
      T_eq about 0 K: P14.T49.i's infrared, which gates T54.a.
    - **7 jumps across the diagonal** (residuals 0.015–0.41), 0.73% of the sample, under the ruling's
      1%:
      - 6 at **the airless threshold** (`AIRLESS_PRESSURE`, 100 Pa): an air of N₂ (93.0 Pa) and Ar
        (7.0 Pa) buffered by its own ices reaches 100 Pa at T_eq 44.74 K. Below it the body is
        `Airless` under its frosts; above it a `Snowball` (or, for one rocky member about an
        evolved host, a `RunawayGreenhouse` at T_s 45.8 K, Venus's deck at 0.76) with its cloud: the
        albedo F jumps between 0.15–0.56 and 0.73–0.99 across one temperature. They are a state
        change of T13.c's at a fixed pressure, so T54.a's cold profile moves them but does not
        remove them; the bisection publishes the threshold's two sides' nearer end, labelled.
        T51.b's record called the class an ice edge of the step cover: it is this state edge.
      - 1 **cover flip** on a 200-bar N₂ and CH₄ snowball at T_eq 112.9 K, T_s 190.6 K (0.68 against
        0.59), the step cover's, for T54.a's cold profile.
  - _The sample test's measures, as built_ (a deviation from "at most 1% is bracketed"): at 23's
    stand-ins 2.1% is bracketed, 8 of them lossless frosts until T49.i, so the test asserts the
    ruling's own escalation measure, at most 1% jumping (0.73%), a 3% guard on all the bracketed,
    every fixed point's residual under 10⁻⁹, every body's T_eq its published albedo's to the bit,
    and at most 57 passes, listing each bracketed body by class. **P14.T54.a's re-check holds the
    bracketed to 1%** at its real inputs (decision-p14-t51-batch §8).
  - _The cost:_ a bracketed body takes 36–56 passes (32 halvings after 4–8 plain passes where a
    2-cycle is found to the bit, and after all 24 for the 3 that find none), against T51.b's 64 at
    the cap, so the sample's passes fall from 4,646 to 4,166 under the batch.
  - _Tests:_ `planetary::derive::passes::tests` (T51.b's loop on stubs; a contracting map, settled
    and, too slow to settle, bracketed; slope −2 banded and to the clamps; the jump; the whole range
    with its upper bound kept, and a kept lower bound taken at the end; ties to the lower albedo;
    two runs; the early stop); `atmosphere::tests::a_body_that_settles_keeps_t51b_s_bits` (above);
    `under_the_batch_the_table_takes_the_area_mix` and the Pluto and Triton recordings now assert
    `Converged`, and the held table `Fixed`; and
    `under_the_batch_the_photometry_states_the_derivation_s_albedo`, the sample's, which derives
    each bracketed body twice and holds the two equal (the sim-determinism skill).
- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)**, from P14.T51.h:
  - _The airless threshold is a step_ (T13.c's `AIRLESS_PRESSURE`, 100 Pa): a body whose
    ice-buffered air crosses it changes state, and its Bond albedo jumps, with no self-consistent
    albedo between (6 of the sample's 954 at 23's stand-ins). A continuous transition, a frost's
    and a thin air's albedos weighed across the threshold, would remove the jump; it is a T13.c
    state-model change, not made here. For P14.T54.a's re-check and P14.T53.c's `Tenuous` state.
  - _A runaway greenhouse at 46 K:_ one rocky member about an evolved host is `RunawayGreenhouse`
    with Venus's full deck at T_s 45.8 K, its insolation once inside the runaway limit at its
    host's largest past luminosity (T13.c's classification), which no cold body's air holds. For
    T13.c's re-validation (P14.T54.a's bless note).
- **Deviations in P14.T51.i, as built (`p14-t51hij`, 2026-10-19).** The cold traps' fast path and
  their pass-invariant field, behind the cold traps' hold (`COLD_TRAPS_VERSION` 24) inside the
  `p14-snapshot` lane's at 23: nothing on the record moves at 22 or 23 (golden_diff: nothing to
  reconcile). The surface crate's half is its own commit, recorded in plan 09 as R09.T7.k, with
  its measured figures.
  - _The choice of rule:_ 8 points (GL-8), 4.4 × 10⁻¹⁶ from 16 points on the ruling's 10,800
    points (its port: 4 × 10⁻¹⁶), and 128 intervals. GL-6 and GL-4 were timed and do not buy the
    budget (below), so the closest rule is kept.
  - _A third lever, bit for bit_ (the ruling's optional "evaluate only where it can bind", in its
    cheapest form): the shared integral skips the bowls shallower than the shallowest that keeps
    any shadow, whose share `read`'s first test makes +0, with a margin of a millionth of the depth
    ratio, far above that test's rounding; neither the bowl nor the density is evaluated there,
    and every sum keeps its bits (`the_skipped_bowls_keep_the_shadow_s_bits`, against the
    unskipped `shadowed` over four bodies, every half degree from 50°, four populations, five
    limits). The cap's own bound and the bisections' closed root, the ruling's other optional
    levers, are not built.
  - _The measured differences_ (the lane's, against 16 points and 512 intervals; plan 09's
    R09.T7.k): the Moon's water −9.3 × 10⁻⁵ (B), +2.8 × 10⁻⁴ (A); its CO₂ at 58.18 K +1.1 × 10⁻³
    (B), +8.5 × 10⁻⁴ (A), and at 10 kg m⁻² Gyr⁻¹'s 55.53 K +2.1 × 10⁻³ and +1.9 × 10⁻³; Mercury's
    water +2.6 × 10⁻⁴; Ceres's shadow at 4° −4.2 × 10⁻⁵ (B), −3.7 × 10⁻⁶ (A), and at 20°
    −2.1 × 10⁻⁴ (A, 52.7 km², under T51.f's 68 km²), beyond the plan's "under 5 × 10⁻⁵", which the
    ruling's port measured at 4° alone. T51.f's tests hold unchanged. R09.T7.d's trapezoid test's
    unit-integrand bound is restated for 128 intervals, 4 × 10⁻⁴ (the rule's h² is 16 times 512
    intervals', whose bound was 5 × 10⁻⁵; 3.2 × 10⁻⁴ measured), and its degree test is the 8-point
    rule's 15; its other tolerances are unchanged.
  - _For R09.T13.f's lane:_ decision-r09-t13f-cold-traps §3.4's tolerance floor of 2 × 10⁻³ assumes
    moves of at most 1.1 × 10⁻³; that holds at `trap_threshold`'s 58.18 K for CO₂, but CO₂ at
    55.53 K moves 2.1 × 10⁻³. T13.f's lane, landing after T51.i, runs its tests on a tip that holds
    T51.i, at §3.4's tolerances.
  - _The regolith's albedo_ is computed in the passes under the batch
    (`DerivedBody::regolith_albedo`, crate-private, with `DerivedMoon`'s, beside `Passes`): the
    passes' regolith provider (`PassSurface::regolith`, `Regolith::of_material` until P14.T54.a's
    lid) at the airless state under the hosts' light, so that T54.a's lid and T54.b's weathering
    reach it with no change. `None` under the held rules, whose passes read no light; a record
    whose derivation gives none keeps P14.T51.a's publish. The record path carries it in the
    surface section's sky (`SurfaceSky::regolith_albedo`) to `condensates_under`, whose cold-trap
    arguments are bundled as `RecordColdTraps` (rules, sky, regolith albedo), a deviation in that
    crate-private signature; `ColdTrapSky`, on R09's interface, is untouched. Under the batch the
    table's Moon, Mercury and Ceres take the Moon's 0.11 to the bit, their area mix's
    (`the_regolith_albedo_is_the_batch_s_bare_ground`).
  - _The field_ (`ColdTrapField`, crate-private): the zonal maxima at the profile's area points and
    each condensable's threshold and f_ct, built by `ColdTrapField::new` from a `Sunlit` and a
    terrain (its f_ct through a `ColdTrapGround`'s `fractions_at`, one call a latitude node for
    every species, each species' sum in `over_latitude`'s order by `over_latitude_each`), or on the
    record path by `ColdTrapField::of`. `publish` tests the body's qualification first
    (`qualifies`: a zonal profile, airless, not collisional) and only then builds the field, once;
    `publish_over(partition, cover, body, field)` is the function T54.b's passes call over one
    field, testing qualification at every call. Where the closed form refuses the ground, the
    field keeps its maxima and every f_ct is 0, as T51.f's traps were. The field's species are the
    record's condensables, water left out on an ice-rich crust; T54.b builds its passes' field over
    a set that does not change between passes (the body's inventory's condensables and the
    delivered species), since the field must hold every condensable a pass's partition names
    (debug-asserted).
  - _The field's carry_ (a deviation from §6's "crate-private on `DerivedBody`"): `DerivedBody`
    carries the regolith's albedo, the input the passes alone know, not the field, whose terrain
    (P14.T48.c's crater contract) and heat flow (P14.T24.b's) are the record path's until P14.T54.a
    and P14.T54.b give them to the passes. The record's `publish` builds its own field, once. T54.b
    builds the passes' field, carries it to `condensates_under`, so that a body builds one, and its
    test counts the builds; `one_field_built_once_serves_every_publish` shows here that one field
    serves every publish.
  - _The trapped part_ (`CondensateEntry::trapped_area_fraction`, public, additive): an inserted
    trap's whole area, a merged one's the trap's area, and where the merge is held to 1 the trap

- **Deviations in P14.T49.h, as built: step 3, the solutions (`p14-liquids`, 2026-10-16).**
  `GENERATOR_VERSION` stays 22. Nothing on the record reads `liquid_properties` before P14.T54.a
  (decision-bump-plan-after-22 §1.2), so `liquids.golden` is re-blessed at 22. Nothing is
  refitted: the 84.5 wt% acid file has been in `liquid_optics` since step 1, so `tables.lock`
  does not move.
  - _Rulings taken_ (decision-p14-t49h-step3-composition, 2026-10-16, on this step's contract
    question and the two choices it recorded):
    - **The naming contract** (§1, §2.1). A component is a registry row that is a neutral species
      with a formula key: `H2O`, `NaCl`, `MgSO4`, `NH3`, `CH4`, `C2H6`, `N2` and `H2SO4`. A
      solution row is never one, and a `Component` enum, a `SoluteKey` and a rowless formula key
      are refused. `H2SO4` is no exception: its row is the molecule, and its liquid columns are
      the aqueous acid's.
    - **The perchlorates have no rows** (§1.3). `brine_naclo4` and `brine_mgclo4` hold their
      solutes' constants in the crate, with no components, and their `Given` is
      `CompositionNotModelled` until `NaClO4` and `Mg(ClO4)2` are appended (Risks, below). The
      ruling has them resolve at `Reference`; with no index they do not (the parts' departures,
      below).
    - **The errors and their order** (§2.3): `NotALiquid`, `CompositionNotModelled`,
      `ComponentNotModelled`, `CompositionOutOfRange`, `OutOfRange`, `NotModelled`, each naming
      the first offence in the given order. A pure row's `Given` is the row at 1, its
      `Reference`; a solution's may name any subset of its components, down to one; a melt's
      stays `CompositionNotModelled`.
    - **Determinism** (§1.5). Every sum runs over the model's own component list in registry
      order, each fraction read from the composition (0 where absent), and `Reference` is the
      path of `Given(reference)`, to the bit.
    - **(a) The range's upper end** (§3) is the lowest critical point among the components the
      composition holds, not the solution's whole list: Titan's reference below N2's 126.192 K, a
      CH4–C2H6 subset below methane's 190.564 K, the brines and the acid below water's 647.096 K
      (their salts and `H2SO4` have no diagram), `nh3_h2o` below NH3's 405.56 K. The lower end
      stays the row's first melt.
    - **(b) No anchor** (§4). A solution's density is its model's at every state, which amends
      decision-p14-t49b-condensed §1.4's "equals" to "agrees within". A test holds each model at
      its fixed value's temperature and the reference composition to §4's tolerances (in kg m⁻³:
      `brine_nacl` ±0.3, `brine_mgso4` ±0.5, the perchlorates ±10 and ±15, `nh3_h2o` ±11, `H2SO4`
      ±0.5, `ch4_c2h6_n2` 0.05), and a miss beyond them is recorded, not anchored away.
  - _The solutions, as built_ (`substance/liquid/solution.rs`; every solution's record is
    `Derived`):
    - **Titan's seas** (`ch4_c2h6_n2`), an ideal mixture of CH4, N2 and C2H6, in registry order:
      - the density by volume additivity, ρ = Σ xᵢ Mᵢ ÷ Σ xᵢ Mᵢ ÷ ρᵢ: 518.87 kg m⁻³ at 93.65 K;
      - the index by Lorentz–Lorenz at that ideal molar volume, from each component's molar
        refraction, in each bin;
      - the surface tension by the Macleod–Sugden parachor in Weinaug and Katz's form, the vapour
        neglected, each parachor from the component's own σ and molar volume at T (15.14 mN m⁻¹
        at 93.65 K, `mixtures.json`);
      - the viscosity by Grunberg–Nissan, every Gᵢⱼ 0 in a table keyed by row pairs, which a test
        holds lists each pair once, so ln μ is the mole-fraction mean (0.197 mPa s at 93.65 K);
      - the absorption by Beer's additivity in volume fractions, absent unless every component
        present has one, so absent while N2's and C2H6's are;
      - the scattering: ES–Cabannes's density term at κ_T,mix = Σ φᵢ κ_T,ᵢ (exact for an ideal
        solution, not the mole-fraction mean), plus an ideal-solution concentration term from
        multinomial composition fluctuations, with one δ, from the mixture's anisotropy ratio and
        `S_iso` = `S_0,mix` (1 + `β_c` ÷ `β_d`), on both terms. It is 6.96 × 10⁻³ and
        2.91 × 10⁻³ m⁻¹ in the bins across 443 and 545 nm at 93.65 K, about half of each the
        concentration term's (the lane's derivation, `step3/mixtures/scripts/mixtures.py`,
        SHA-256 7f0b8304…);
      - the reference mole fractions, held as the derivation's exact values (0.739146, 0.164352
        and 0.096503 to six decimals), since the six-decimal ones sum to 1.000001, which
        `LiquidComposition::new` refuses; a test recomputes them from Mastrogiuseppe et al.'s
        71/12/17 vol%;
      - each component below its triple point (methane's 90.694 K and ethane's 90.368 K lie inside
        the range from 71.15 K) by decision-p14-t49b-condensed §2.5: the density's line, the index
        carried to it, κ_T held at the triple point, step 2's VFT viscosity, Mulero's σ and the
        file's absorption held, each `Derived` and tested continuous at the triple point.
    - **The chloride and sulphate brines** (`brine_nacl`, `brine_mgso4`), aqueous electrolytes of
      water and the salt row, each member water's own record with the salt's empirical term:
      - the density Laliberté and Cooper 2004's apparent specific volume (their supporting
        information's coefficients), with the sim's water in place of theirs (its ancillary;
        below 273.16 K §2.5's line);
      - the viscosity Laliberté 2007's, ln μ by mass fraction of water's and the salt's term
        (MgSO4's the corrected set), with the sim's R12-08 water;
      - the index by additivity of specific refraction by mass, each salt's from the
        International Critical Tables vol. VII's air-relative tables taken to vacuum (Ciddor's
        standard air): NaCl 1.582 06 × 10⁻⁴ m³ kg⁻¹ at 589.3 nm (±0.3%), MgSO4 1.162 65 × 10⁻⁴
        (±2%). Its dispersion is a stand-in shaped on Quan and Fry 1995's seawater (+4.4% at
        380 nm, −1.9% at 780 nm), since a constant one gives the increment the opposite slope;
      - the absorption: NaCl's is water's at its volume fraction, the salt transparent (Röttgers,
        McKee and Utschig 2014's sea salt); MgSO4's is absent;
      - σ and b absent;
      - the composition from water alone to the density fit's top fraction (NaCl x 0.097867,
        w 0.2603; MgSO4 x 0.049961, w 0.26), and the temperature from the eutectic (251.9 and
        269.29 K) to below 647.096 K, each empirical member `Derived` outside its fit (the
        densities 0–140 and 0–125 °C, the viscosities 5–154 and 15–150 °C);
      - the references the eutectics' 23.3 wt% NaCl and 17.30 wt% MgSO4, x 0.085627 and 0.030360.
    - **The perchlorate brines** (`brine_naclo4`, `brine_mgclo4`), `AwaitingSolute`: their
      solutes' elements and molar masses held (122.436 and 223.197 g mol⁻¹, IUPAC 2021's abridged
      weights, tested), and the stated density at every temperature (1,445 and 1,394 kg m⁻³),
      `Derived` away from its state. With no index the record is `NotModelled` for
      `RefractiveIndex` from the eutectic to below water's 647.096 K, and `OutOfRange` outside,
      the range checked first.
    - **Ammonia–water** (`nh3_h2o`), evaluated at its reference composition only (the eutectic's
      0.321 NH3 by mass, x 0.333364): the density held at the stated 946 kg m⁻³ (Hammond,
      Parmentier and Barr 2018, after Croft et al. 1988), `Derived` away from 176.15 K; the index
      by Lorentz–Lorenz and σ by the parachor, both at that density's molar volume from water's
      and ammonia's records, each below its triple point by §2.5 (1.3814 in the bin across
      545 nm and 83.8 mN m⁻¹ at 176.15 K); μ, a and b absent. Any other composition, beyond

    - **The aqueous acid** (`H2SO4`), water and the acid's own row, 25–85 wt% (`H2SO4` x
      0.057698–0.510025), its reference 75.0 wt% (x 0.355286 with the row's 98.072 g mol⁻¹), from
      its 233.67 K first melt to below water's 647.096 K:
      - the density Myhre, Nielsen and Saastad 1998's Eq. 2 with its printed T⁴ column dropped,
        32 terms (chempy's transcription, matched by aerosolpy's and, but k₆,₁, CARMA's):

      - the index by specific refraction linear in mass fraction between Palmer and Williams

      - the absorption by Beer's additivity by mass of the two files' upper bounds between them,
        and outside them the larger mass coefficient held (75 wt%'s in every bin), so it steps at

        decision-p14-t49b-condensed §1.4's volume-fraction Beer additivity up to the mixture's
        excess volume, the two end members being solutions of the same pair rather than pure

      - σ Vehkamäki et al. 2002's Eq. 9, standing in for Myhre's own: 71.30 mN m⁻¹ at 80 wt% and

      - μ Williams and Long 1995's (as Shi et al. 2001 and three model codes print it), W held in

      This retires step 1's deferred finding that the acid's index and density are held at their

  - _The parts' departures._
    - **The perchlorate brines do not resolve.** No specific refraction of NaClO₄ or Mg(ClO₄)₂ was
      read, so their `Reference` answers `NotModelled { RefractiveIndex }` from the eutectic to
      below 647.096 K. This departs from the ruling's "resolve at `Reference`" and from the
      entry's "every liquid-range row has n and ρ", which skips them. No producer reaches them
      before 24 (decision-p14-t49h-step3-composition §1.3).
    - **Water's viscosity below 273.16 K**, where R12-08 is not evaluated and water has no
      supercooled form, is Laliberté's water equation (as `thermo` writes it, citing
      Laliberté 2009) scaled to R12-08 at 273.16 K, a factor of 1.000 67, so a brine's viscosity
      is continuous there (tested within 10⁻⁶); an unchecked extrapolation, `Derived`.
    - **The mixture's `S_0`** takes each component equation's own specific gas constant by mass
      fraction, exact in the pure limit; it lies 3 × 10⁻⁵ from the research's `k_B` `N_A` ÷ M̄.
    - **The 10⁻⁹ composition slack** (`MOLE_FRACTION_SLACK`, `LiquidComposition::new`'s sum
      tolerance) applies to every model's range, so a composition converted by other arithmetic

    - **The components are fixed registry indices** in `rows/liquids.rs` (`WATER_ID`, row 2, to
      `MAGNESIUM_SULPHATE_ID`, row 100), append-only, each tied to its key by a test.

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)**, from P14.T49.h's step 3:
  - _Titan's density_ is ideal mixing's, 1.4–1.9% low against the measured excess volumes of Hiza,
    Haynes and Parrish 1977 and Hiza and Haynes 1980 (reprinted in NBS Monograph 172, read; −2.65%
    for a Titan-like ternary at 105 K): about 526–529 kg m⁻³ at Ligeia, against 518.9. So its index
    is about 0.004–0.005 low (molar refraction is additive with the real volume) and its parachor
    σ about 6–8% low. Ideal mixing stands, as ruled (decision-p14-t49b-condensed §1.2).
  - _Titan's viscosity_ takes every Grunberg–Nissan Gᵢⱼ 0: Diller 1982 and 1984 and Friend 1990
    are closed and unread. |G| ≤ 0.5 would move μ by ±11% at Ligeia's composition (|G| ≤ 1,
    ±21%). Tan, Kargel and Marion 2013, the cross-check decision-r11-palette-liquids §1.8 names, is
    closed and unread.
  - _Titan's scattering_: the ideal-solution concentration term about doubles b (2.9 times pure
    methane's at 545 nm; the term is 1.1 times the density term at 93.65 K, 1.5 times at 71 K). It
    is a lower bound, CH4–N2 deviating positively from Raoult's law. Kirkwood and Goldberg 1950
    and Stockmayer 1950 (the fluctuations), and Coumou, Mackor and Hijmans 1964, Kerker 1969 and
    Bhatia and Thornton 1970 (a binary's Rayleigh ratio), are unread.
  - _Titan's upper range_: ideal mixing carries N2's near-critical κ_T, so b grows 1.7 times by
    110 K and 4.4 times by 120 K, which a real dilute-N2 solution would not show; the `q_max` ξ
    rule acts only within about 0.4 K of 126.192 K. The fixed composition above 93.65 K is a
    stand-in: at 1.5 bar the liquid is at its bubble point there and would lose N2. A sourced
    bound needs a bubble-point model and the surface pressure (GERG-2008, Risks above).
  - _Titan's surface tension_: the parachor's variants span 15.04–15.62 mN m⁻¹ against the built
    15.14 at 93.65 K (two of them on parachors from memory). Against Baidakov et al. 2011's
    measured CH4–N2 (closed; read off Kumar and Chevrier 2020's figures, arXiv:2002.07126) it meets
    an N2 mole fraction of 0.18 at 105 K to 0.0% and is 6.6% high at 0.437 and 95 K. With Jasper's
    methane (step 2's conflict) the mixture would be about 6% higher. Macleod 1923, Sugden 1924,
    Weinaug and Katz 1943, Grunberg and Nissan 1949 and Poling, Prausnitz and O'Connell are cited,
    their texts unread.
  - _Ammonia–water_: Croft, Lunine and Kargel 1988 and Kargel et al. 1991 are closed and unread, so
    its density is held at 946 kg m⁻³ (Hammond, Parmentier and Barr 2018's text; their own Eq. 12,
    a fit along the liquidus, gives 957), its viscosity is absent (their Eq. 13 gives 2.75 Pa s
    against their text's about 5) and only its reference composition is evaluated. Its σ by the
    parachor at T is 83.8 mN m⁻¹, against 76.8 with the components' triple-point parachors, and is
    probably high (ammonia's enrichment at the surface; King, Hall and Ware 1930 and Rice 1928 are
    closed). No measured index of concentrated aqueous ammonia was reached (ICT VII holds
    0.5–1 N). Ideal volume additivity would be 4.6% low (902 kg m⁻³). κ_T is unsourced, so b is
    absent. At one atmosphere the 32 wt% liquid boils near room temperature, far below the
    range's 405.56 K.
  - _The brines' densities_ miss T49.b's fixed values at their states by +0.735 (NaCl) and
    −2.165 kg m⁻³ (MgSO4), beyond ±0.3 and ±0.5: pinned, not anchored (ruling §4). The ICT values
    are likely the better: the model sits 0.76–0.88 above ICT's NaCl at 22–24 wt% and 1.7–2.3
    below its MgSO4 at 16–18 wt% at 0 °C, yet meets its MgSO4 at 20 °C within 0.22, a bias at the
    fits' lowest temperature. Laliberté's 2004, 2007 and 2009 sets agree within 0.07 for NaCl but
    spread 3.7 kg m⁻³ for MgSO4.
  - _The brines' water below 0 °C_ is §2.5's line: at the NaCl eutectic, 251.9 K, it gives 998.34
    against Kell's 992.69 (Laliberté and Cooper's water), so the brine is about 6 kg m⁻³ high
    there.
  - _The brines' viscosities_ below 5 °C (NaCl) and 15 °C (MgSO4) are extrapolations: NaCl's meets
    ICT V's 0 °C data within +0.8 to +1.6%; MgSO4's and both eutectics' are unchecked, and below
    273.16 K they rest on Laliberté's water equation (Laliberté 2009 unread; its form as `thermo`
    writes it) extrapolated into supercooled water. Laliberté 2007's "Additions and Corrections",
    MgSO4's set, is unread as text.
  - _The brines' surface tension_ is absent: Dutcher, Wexler and Clegg 2010 is closed. Its authors'
    E-AIM evaluation, reduced in the lane's scratch (`step3/brines/`, to 0.04 and 0.007 mN m⁻¹),
    would be an offline fit for `hyperion-fit`. E-AIM misses ICT IV by −0.26 to −0.46 mN m⁻¹, and
    its supercooled water lies 0.886 mN m⁻¹ above R1-76 at 251.9 K, so a fit would apply E-AIM's
    increments to the sim's water.
  - _The brines' scattering_ is absent, their compressibility unsourced: Rogers and Pitzer 1982 and
    Archer 1992 for NaCl are leads not transcribed; Millero, Ward, Lepple and Hoff 1974 for MgSO4
    is closed.
  - _The brines' optics_: NaCl's absorption extrapolates sea salt's transparency (Röttgers, McKee
    and Utschig 2014, its abstract read and its coefficients through WOPP v3, at S about 40) to
    the eutectic's 233 g kg⁻¹ (about −6% to +5% of water's at 700–750 nm, extrapolated linearly);
    MgSO4's absorption is absent; MgSO4's refraction is ±2% from one 1 N point (ICT VII, 5.7 wt%)
    extrapolated to 17.3 wt%, its dispersion NaCl's stand-in; NaCl's own dispersion (Tan and
    Huang 2015) is unread.
  - _The seawater oracle_: a 3.5 wt% NaCl brine's increment in the bin across 545 nm at 25 °C is
    +0.006 06 against Quan and Fry's +0.006 39 at S = 35, sea salt being about 78% NaCl by mass: a
    composition effect, not a model miss.
  - _The perchlorate brines_ have no index, viscosity, absorption, compressibility or temperature
    law of density: Hnědkovský and Hefter 2021 (NaClO4's density, closed), Lumme 1970 and the index
    and viscosity leads in their sources (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 79, 1789; Fajans and Johnson 1942;
    Lumme and Högnäs 1968; Miller and Doran 1956; Janz et al. 1970; Toner et al. 2014) are unread.
  - _The acid's density_: Myhre et al. 1998's printed T⁴ column is wrong (+7.1 kg m⁻³ at 75 wt% and
    300 K and +85 at 323 K against the ICT) and is dropped. Oca et al. 2018 report Lund Myhre et
    al. 2003's refit with powers of t to 3, which is closed and unread. Above about 390 K at 25–40
    and 84.5–85 wt% the cubic in t turns over and the density rises again, far beyond its fit.
  - _The acid's surface tension_: Myhre et al. 1998's own fit, the ruled source, is unread;
    Vehkamäki et al. 2002 stands in, +0.19 mN m⁻¹ on Myhre's 71.11 at 80 wt% and 273 K.
  - _The acid's viscosity above 80 wt%_ holds W at 80 (UKCA's rule), 15% under the ICT vol. V at
    84.5 wt% and 25 °C; the cubics extrapolated would be 32% over (the ICT's ratio there is 1.163),
    and the research's lean, 80 wt%'s value times that ratio, was not taken. Williams and Long 1995
    and Shi et al. 2001 are closed, read through CAM, GEOS-Chem and UKCA; Das et al. 1997 is
    unread.
  - _The acid's index_: Palmer and Williams's visible n sits about +0.006 above Biermann and Luo's
    at 75 wt% and 610 nm, and +0.009 above the ICT's at 95.6 wt%; at 80 wt% the rule meets
    Biermann's within 10⁻⁴. Extrapolated to 25–50 wt% it misses Palmer and Williams's own files by
    −0.013 to −0.006 at 359.7–449.4 nm (within ±0.005 at 555.6–701.8 nm). Luo, Krieger and Peter
    1996 is closed.
  - _The acid's molar mass_ is the registry's 98.072 g mol⁻¹ (IUPAC 2021), not the research brief's
    98.079: the reference's mole fraction moves by 2 × 10⁻⁵.
  - _The acid's compressibility_ is unsourced (Valleau 1965, closed), so b is absent.
  - _Not from this change_: `cargo doc -p hyperion-sim` with `-D warnings` fails on broken
    intra-doc links in the galaxy, planetary, sky and stellar modules.
- **Deviations in P14.T49.h, as built: step 4, the melts (`p14-liquids`, 2026-10-16).**
  `GENERATOR_VERSION` stays 22. Nothing on the record reads `liquid_properties` or
  `tables::liquid_optics` before P14.T54.a (decision-bump-plan-after-22 §1.2), so `liquids.golden`
  is re-blessed at 22, and `liquid_optics` refitted by decision-p14-t49h-liquids §5 for R08's
  basaltic glass.
  - _Rulings taken_ (decision-p14-t49h-step4-melts, 2026-10-16, on this step's finding):
    - **The two Al-rich rows take Giordano and Russell 2007's model** (GR07; J. Phys.: Condens.
      Matter 19, 205148, Table 1's VFT column), a deviation from the entry's "Giordano et al.'s":
      log₁₀ μ = −4.67 + B ÷ (T − C) on SiO₂, Al₂O₃, MgO and CaO in mol%, FeO(T) and MnO as MgO
      mole for mole, Na₂O, K₂O, TiO₂, Cr₂O₃ and P₂O₅ dropped and the four renormalised, `Derived`
      at every temperature. Giordano, Russell and Dingwell 2008 (GRD) is 2.5 log units low on
      Scarfe et al. 1983's anorthite at 1,600 °C (−2.09 against 0.43 log Pa s): its Al₂O₃ term is
      negative, and the alkali-balanced term that offsets it is zero in an alkali-free melt (§1).
    - **Not Scarfe's fits** (§2.1, §4). Their Fulcher T₀ lies 110–130 K too high, so beyond their
      spans (1,648–1,898 and 1,573–1,873 K) they run 0.5 log units too viscous at 2,400 K and 0.96
      at 3,000 K against GR07; a measured analogue's fit would be `StandIn`, never `Measured` (§5).
    - **The selection rule** (§2.3): a melt takes GR07 where its oxides hold Al₂O₃ ≥ 15 wt%,
      Na₂O + K₂O ≤ 1 wt% and at most 3 wt% of the oxides the mapping drops; any other melt GRD.
      Today it selects exactly `anorthosite` (Al₂O₃ 34.0, alkalis 0.53) and `feldspathic` (27.3,
      0.63). A melt that meets the first two but not the third is a question for main, so its
      viscosity is absent (`MeltViscosityModel::Unruled`); no row is there.
    - **TiO₂'s volume** (§6): 23.16 cm³ mol⁻¹ at 1,673 K with dV/dT 7.246 × 10⁻³ cm³ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹
      (MELTS's `liq_struct_data.h`, "2.316 J/bar, Lange and Carmichael (1990)"; Ghiorso and
      Kress 2004's 23.448 corroborates it). DensityX's 28.32 at 1,773 K is another set's, recorded.
  - _The rows' oxides_ (weight per cent; `substance/rows/melts.rs`, each with its source and
    basis, and its GRD calibration where it lies outside):
    - `basalt`: Alae lava lake's bulk (Peck 1978, USGS Professional Paper 935-B, p. B3), the row's
      own source, its eleven oxides summing to 100.00;
    - `lava_glass`: `basalt`'s, adopted (the glass is the quenched melt);

- **Deferred findings (2026-10-13 rule)**, from P14.T49.h's step 4:
  - _GRD's calibration_ (K₂O 0.3–9, FeO(T) 0–12, MgO 0–32 wt%) excludes the lunar, Mercury and
    komatiite melts by K₂O, `basalt_fe` (20.2) and `komatiite` (12.9) by FeO(T), and `ultramafic`
    (37.8) by MgO. GR07 with the same mapping agrees within 0.5 log units there (the ruling's §7:
    G2 0.22, G1 0.16, 15597 0.15, a peridotite 0.29, komatiite 0.47), consistency rather than
    validation. Its two follow-ups: Murase and McBirney 1970's Apollo 11 high-Ti synthetic (0.45
    Pa s at 1,495 °C, Lunar Sourcebook §6.1.1) as a check of GRD on Fe-rich melts; Mercury's rows
    carry no Na₂O, where MESSENGER's gamma-ray spectrometer found several weight per cent (on
    Vetere et al. 2017's Na-rich analogue GRD is 0.06 log units low against measurement).
  - _The melt's redox moves ρ by about 2%_: on the Columbia River basalt, Lange and Carmichael's
    is 1.6–2.7% above Murase's densities (Bottinga and Weill 1970, Fig. 2) with the rock's own
    Fe₂O₃/FeO, and +1.2 to +0.1% with all iron as Fe₂O₃. Kress and Carmichael 1991 at T50.a's
    oxygen fugacity would set the ratio.
  - _TiO₂'s volume_: 23.16 against DensityX's 28.32 moves Alae's ρ by 0.4%; Lange and Carmichael
    1987's own fit is unread.
  - _At the solidus the record is the bulk liquid_, not the crystal-laden residual melt: Shaw et
    al. 1968 give 8,000 poise for the Makaopuhi suspension at 1,130 °C against 4,000 for its
    liquid.
  - _A water term_: 0.1 wt% H₂O would lower granite's μ by 0.26 log units in GRD; the record's
    melts are anhydrous unless it carries dissolved water, an ask of T51.
  - _A composition-general melt index_ (Gladstone–Dale or oxide refractivities, Mandarino 1976
    and 1981, from memory) is deferred; the glass's is held. Carried by Lorentz–Lorenz with Alae
    glass's assumed 2,760 kg m⁻³ it would give `basalt` 1.553 at 550 nm and 1,473 K (normal
    Fresnel reflectance 0.0469 against the held 0.0489).

      alone. The sim's `a_snapshot_is_body_at_body_by_body` holds the same list over 80 systems.

      bodies'.
